items.title: 2026 Banko Gotiti; Second Selection - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our second selection of the season from the Banko Gotiti washing station in Gedeb. The site had an exceptional year, and we are glad to be able to share this second lot with you. In the cup we find nectarine, soft florals, and clementine.

items.title: 2026 Keramo - Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot comes from the extreme elevation of Karamo Village in the Bura zone of Sidama. The site is new to us, but we know and love the region. In the cup we find ripe berries, peach, and honeysuckle.

items.title: 2026 Flor Marina Betancourt; Finca Cataluña, First Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is our second release from Flor Marina, but the first of this new harvest cycle. Palestina produces some of our favorite Pink Bourbon profiles in Huila and we're excited for the opportunity to work with her coffee again this season. In the cup, we find raspberry, tangerine, and rosehips.

items.title: 2026 Juan Pablo Luque; Whua Whua Yoc, Competition Lot - Peru
items.desc: This was our highest-scoring lot in a local competition held near Inkawasi. In the cup we find orange blossom and complex tropical fruit, with exceptional structure.

items.title: 2026 Juan Carlos Gomez; Finca La Esperanza, First Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: Juan Carlos is a new producer in our Huila project, and this is our first time working with his coffee. In the cup we find Key lime pie, blueberry, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Luis & Mildred Montoya; Finca Arboleda, First Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: We purchased our first lot from Luis this spring, and we are excited to welcome him back to the menu. Producing one exceptional lot in a year is challenging, and doing it twice is impressive. As our project in Urrao continues to thrive, we look forward to seeing what 2027 brings. In the cup we find a tropical profile of passion fruit, lemon zest, and cranberry.

items.title: 2026 Tamiru Tadesse Tesema; Safo, Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is an exceptional separation from Alo's Safo site. The cherry comes from extreme altitudes and is a staggering example of the quality this special place can produce. In the cup we find a floral expression of honeysuckle, bergamot, nectarine, and silver needle.

items.title: 2026 Harold Ortiz Ceron; Finca La Cava, Chiroso - Colombia
items.desc: This is our second lot from Harold Ortiz Ceron, a new producer in San Pablo, Nariño. This Chiroso separation is the first Chiroso we have ever released from San Pablo. In the cup we find ripe strawberry, tangerine, and oolong.

items.title: 2026 Harold Ortiz Ceron; Finca La Cava, Pink Bourbon - Colombia
items.desc: This is a special release, as it is rare to see Pink Bourbon being cultivated in Nariño. We are honored to have been introduced to Harold Ceron, who is now producing many exceptional varieties on his new farm. In the cup we find blueberry, blood orange, and raspberry.

items.title: 2026 Chelbessa; 2nd Selection - Ethiopia
items.desc: Chelbessa has long been one of our favorite sites to work with in Gedeb, and we are pleased to welcome this year’s selection to the menu. In the cup we find stone fruit, citrus, and lemon verbena.

items.title: 2026 Sike Bokasso, White Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: Sike Bokasso produces some of our favorite coffees in Guji, and this white honey preparation is no exception. In the cup we find melon, candied peach, and star fruit.

items.title: 2026 Elpidio Tabares; La Soledad - Colombia
items.desc: One of the longest and best seasons we have ever seen in Urrao has also brought new growth to our project there. In this lot, our first from Elpidio Tabares, we find passion fruit, lychee, and citrus.

items.title: 2026 Eulises Fabian Quilindo; El Higueron - Colombia
items.desc: This continues our slow shift toward the southern Huila season, and the exploration of the new Santa María region. In the cup we find bright red berries, lime, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2026 Kanzu; Lot #16 - Rwanda
items.desc: This is our first release of the upcoming Rwandan season. We look forward to these coffees every year, and this lot is a fitting start. In the cup we find mulling spices, orange peel, and baked fruit.

items.title: 2026 Demeka Becha, Dry-Fermented - Ethiopia
items.desc: The Demeka site has produced some truly exceptional coffees over the years. This year, we selected exceptional dry-fermented and wet-fermented lots. In the cup we find lychee, black tea, and raspberry.

items.title: 2026 Pepe Jijon; Finca Soledad, TyOxy - Ecuador
items.desc: Pepe brings an artist’s intuition to his coffee, and this TyOxy lot is another stunning expression of his work. Compared with previous lots, it reveals a softer, more delicate side of a profile we have come to know well. In the cup we find hibiscus, the sparkling acidity of raspberry and tree tomato, and a subtle hint of fig.

items.title: David Berrio; La Casita, Curtain Call - Colombia
items.desc: This is the latest in the year we have ever received a harvest delivery from Urrao, and it comes from David Berrio. The quality has matched the occasion, and we are grateful this season has continued to deliver. In the cup we find nectarine, passion fruit, and honeysuckle.

items.title: 2026 Victor Dota, 2nd Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This Discord-exclusive lot from Victor Dota is exceptionally small, coming from his tiny 0.5-hectare (1.2-acre) farm. This coffee was taken straight off of the drying beds and flown to New York immediately. In the cup we find lemon zest, floral botanicals, and ripe stone fruit.

items.title: 2026 Pepe & Family; Finca Soledad Sidra Wave Natural, New Season - Ecuador
items.desc: This naturally processed Sidra comes from our dear friends Pepe and Jose Jijón, sourced exclusively for espresso for our collaboration with Motors. In the cup we find fruit punch, pineapple, and mango.

items.title: 2026 Morgan Family x Lost Origin; Gales - Panama
items.desc: Our second lot of the year from Lost Origin is a stunning expression of Gesha. In the cup we find a very floral-forward profile of mango, lychee, and jasmine.

items.title: 2026 Duber Mejia; El Diamante, Surprise Encore - Colombia
items.desc: This was our first year working with Duber Mejia's coffees, and it has been remarkable. He has produced some of our top-scoring lots from Urrao, and this last surprise delivery was a welcome one. In the cup we find tropical fruit, soft florals, and sparkling acidity.

items.title: 2026 Luz Stella Rivera; El Oregon - Colombia
items.desc: This lot continues our exploration of Santa María in Huila. It is our first year working with Luz Rivera, and we are pleased to have the opportunity to showcase this lot. In the cup we find raspberry, citrus, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2026 Halo Hartume; 2nd Selection - Ethiopia
items.desc: Halo Hartume has become an integral part of our work in Gedeb, and it is an honor to continue working with these coffees. Halo Hartume not only produces exceptional coffee, but the site also helps process cherry from isolated areas nearby. In the cup we find melon, plum, and lemon verbena.

items.title: 2026 Geshe - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a new separation from the Chorso woreda (district), processed at the Halo washing station. Our thanks go out to SNAP for helping bring this lot together. In the cup we find peach blossom, nectarine, and lemon.

items.title: 2026 Faiber Rodriguez; Finca Guatemala, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This lot marks the beginning of the new harvest season in Colombia, and we are eager to share our first lot from Faiber Rodriguez with the world. In the cup we find refined citrus acidity, strawberry, and white grape.

items.title: 2026 Hermilda Zapata; El Rosal - Colombia
items.desc: It is our first year working with Hermilda Zapata. Hermilda planted her 100% Chiroso plot in 2023, and we are eager to see how this very young farm progresses. In the cup we find lychee, plum, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2026 Diana Alviz; Los Guayabos - Colombia
items.desc: This is a new lot in our ongoing exploration of the Pink Bourbon variety. Each season, it is remarkable to see how this project continues to shift and grow, and we are pleased to see it expanding into Tolima. In the cup we find candied pomelo, berries, and fig.

items.title: 2026 Nicolas Medina; El Girasol - Colombia
items.desc: This farm, historically run by Nicolas’s son Abelardo, has produced some of the most dynamic and intense expressions of Pink Bourbon that we have tasted from Huila. This lot is no different. In the cup we find ripe blackberry, hibiscus, and lime zest.

items.title: 2026 Victor Dota; End Of Season - Ecuador
items.desc: As the Ecuadorian season starts to come to a close, we are pleased to release this last harvest from Victor Dota. In the cup we find dried strawberry, floral botanicals, and lemon.

items.title: 2026 Guiliar Pérez Cuéllar; La Granja, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is the second harvest pass that we have purchased from Guiliar Cuéllar this season. He is an inspiring new producer who has now produced two exceptional lots. In the cup we find lemonade, hibiscus, and mulberry.

items.title: 2026 Tuke Yute; Keramo, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing a lot from Tuke Yute in Keramo, Bensa. We have been inspired by his coffees for a couple of years now and are pleased to finally release one. In the cup we find a fruit-forward profile of strawberry jam, lychee, and rose.

items.title: 2026 Yaye Arbegona - Ethiopia
items.desc: Arbegona holds a very special place in our hearts, and each year we look forward to fall when we finally get to release these high-elevation lots from this remarkable region. In the cup we find watermelon, a lovely florality, and berries.

items.title: 2026 Yana Milena Quintero; Lote 1 - Colombia
items.desc: This is a new selection continuing our exploration of Santa María, Huila. Yana has a stunning Pink Bourbon garden, and we are pleased to be working with her coffee for the first time. In the cup we find rose hips, tangerine, and mulberry.

items.title: 2026 Kedida Gubata - Ethiopia
items.desc: Kedida Gubata is a new high-elevation separation from our export partners at SNAP. Now in our second year working with them on this lot, we decided to try it as a white honey process. In the cup we find honeydew, peach, and coffee blossom.

items.title: 2026 Tamiru Tadesse Tasema; Safo, Hybrid Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: Made for us by our dear friend Tamiru Tadesse, this special hybrid washed lot comes from his main site in the town of Alo, Bensa. In the cup we find tropical fruit, candied peach, rose, and berries.

items.title: 2026 Chorso Bule; Highest Elevation Project - Ethiopia
items.desc: Together with our friends at SNAP, we made this separation by requesting only the cherry grown above 2,450 meters. SNAP is calling this the Highest Elevation Project, and we are deeply grateful to everyone who brought it together. In the cup we find ripe peach, melon, and honeysuckle.

items.title: 2026 Daniel Caro Lopez; El Tambo, End Of Season - Colombia
items.desc: This season brought some of the highest-quality Chiroso lots we have seen from our project in northern Antioquia. Daniel Caro's last harvest of the season is a lovely end to an exceptional year. In the cup we find lychee, oolong, and mango.

items.title: 2026 Luis Muños; El Porvenir - Colombia
items.desc: This lot from the talented young producer Luis Muños is the first from a new project underway in Gaitania. In the cup we find ripe berries, tamarind, and lime zest.

items.title: 2026 Jose Jijon; Finca Soledad Zero, New Season - Ecuador
items.desc: This is Jose’s first time producing coffee at Finca Soledad using a processing method entirely of his own design. He named this lot Zero, marking the beginning of a new series of processing experiments. In the cup we find blackcurrant jam, pomegranate, and a lingering floral finish reminiscent of high-mountain oolong.

items.title: 2026 Mbature Family; Kamavindi Estate, Lot #2 - Kenya
items.desc: This is our second release of the season from Kamavindi. Kamavindi is one of our main collaborators in Kenya, and the center of our ongoing exploration of Kenyan varieties and lot separations. In the cup we find rose hips, candied orange, and currants.

items.title: 2026 Danche, 2nd Selection - Ethiopia
items.desc: One of our longest-standing partnerships in Gedeb, Ethiopia, the Danche site continues to be a source of exceptional coffee. This is our second selection from Danche this season. In the cup we find bergamot, watermelon, and peach.

items.title: 2026 Digna Nuñez x Lost Origin - Panama
items.desc: This is our second year working with Digna's Lost Origin coffee. This lot is thoughtfully crafted, specifically made with tremendous care and intentionality for our collaboration with Motors. In the cup we find strawberry Jolly Rancher, jasmine, and rose. Each box is hand-painted, making each one completely unique.

items.title: 2026 David Berrio; La Casita, Surprise Encore - Colombia
items.desc: One of the longest harvest seasons we have ever seen in Urrao has also been one of the most exceptional for quality. This encore harvest delivery from David Berrio came as a wonderful surprise. In the cup we find peach, melon, red tea, and lovely florality.

items.title: 2026 Lizeth Samboni; La Esmeralda - Colombia
items.desc: It has been remarkable to see the diversification of varieties cultivated in the Huila region over the last few years. Sidra is still rare in Colombia, but exploring different varieties has been instrumental in the elevated quality we have seen from these talented producers. In the cup we find soft botanicals, nectarine, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2026 Blanca Ligia Riascos; Cumbre - Colombia
items.desc: Blanca Ligia Riascos has produced an exceptional Gesha from one of the more remote growing regions in Colombia: Nariño. In the cup we find lovely florality, citrus, and peach.

items.title: 2026 Alejandrina Maytan; Kukipata - Peru
notes: With a soft but lifting acidity
items.desc: This is our last Peru SL9* of this season. These coffees have completely redefined the global coffee landscape for us and have emphatically put Peru on the map as being capable of producing some of the best coffees in the world. In the cup we find a more fruit-forward and jammy profile of yellow tropical fruit and strawberry, with a soft but lifting acidity.

items.title: 2026 Mate Matiwos; Keramo - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first year working with the coffee from Mate Matiwos, and we are grateful for all of the love and intentionality that went into bringing this coffee to us. In the cup we find berries, tropical fruit, and bergamot.

items.title: 2026 Susan Meneses - Colombia
items.desc: We do not currently buy much coffee from San Adolfo, but this lot from Susan Meneses is a standout. We look forward to visiting and learning more on our next trip to Huila. In this cup we find hibiscus, blueberry, and finger lime.

items.title: 2026 Gerald Njagi; Kambarare - Kenya
items.desc: This lot is the main SL* separation from Gerald's main plot of Kambarare. Gerald is one of the most impressive Kenyan producers we have met, and this is his second year working with us on the Retro 1984 project. It is an honor to continue working with this separation. In the cup we find hibiscus, grapefruit, and currants.

items.title: 2026 Carmen Montoya; Bella Vista - Colombia
items.desc: Carmen Montoya produced the first Chiroso that we ever tasted from Urrao a number of years ago. Her coffee sparked our curiosity about this variety and region, and it feels like a full circle to have the opportunity to work with her coffee again. In the cup we find plum, mulberry, and candied lemon.

items.title: 2026 Demeka Becha - Ethiopia
items.desc: The Demeka site has produced some truly exceptional coffees over the years. We do not buy much coffee from Bona Zuria, but Demeka has consistently produced some compelling profiles. In the cup we find pineapple, Earl Grey tea, and jasmine.

items.title: 2026 Sike Bokasso - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our second year working with coffee from Sike Bokasso. Guji has had an unbelievable year, and we are thrilled to welcome this coffee back to the menu. In the cup we find watermelon, peach, and lemongrass.

items.title: 2026 Harmufo - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a separation of only the highest elevation cherry from around Harmufo. We have been interested in this area for some time, and our exporting partner, SNAP, graciously helped make this lot possible. In the cup we find lemon candy, ripe stone fruit, and honeydew.

items.title: 2026 Guiliar Pérez Cuéllar; La Granja - Colombia
items.desc: We started focusing a little more on the region of Santa Maria in Huila last year. Guiliar Cuéllar is a new producer for us, and we are eager to see this region continue to grow. In the cup we find lemonade, fresh blueberry, and subtle florality.

items.title: 2026 Mbature Family; Kamavindi Estate, Gesha - Kenya
items.desc: This is our third year having the privilege of working with Kamavindi’s Gesha separation, and we are delighted to share it exclusively with our subscribers. We continue to learn a great deal about this particular plot and variety. This year's selection leans in a more botanical direction. In the cup we find sencha, white florals, and melon.

items.title: 2026 Abraham Armijos - Ecuador
items.desc: This is our first year working with Abraham Armijos. Mejorado has long been one of our favorite varieties to work with in Ecuador, and this is an exceptional expression of the variety. In the cup we find lemon zest, peach, and wild strawberry.

items.title: 2026 Kamwangi - Kenya
items.desc: We have been working with the Kamwangi site for a number of years now, and it continues to produce some of the highest-quality coffees in all of Kenya. In the cup we find cranberry, raspberry, and rose hips.

items.title: 2026 Yabitu Koba - Ethiopia
items.desc: We are pleased to welcome Yabitu Koba back to our lineup. It has been a few years since we purchased a coffee from the south of Ethiopia. Uraga used to play an extremely important role in our coffee sourcing, and it is gratifying to be working within the area again. In the cup we find peach candy, lemon zest, and florality.

items.title: 2026 Pepe & Jose Jijón And Francisco Vintimilla; Putushio, 2nd Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: Pepe and Jose created this special lot after cupping through many selections to assemble the best of what Putushio produced this year. In the cup we find orange blossom, mandarin, and cooked pear.

items.title: 2026 William Ortiz; La Cabaña, End Of Season - Colombia
items.desc: The third and final harvest pass of William Ortiz's Chiroso closes out our first year working with his coffees—and they have, without question, been some of the best coffees of the year. In the cup we find a softer yet complex tropical profile with melon and lime.

items.title: 2026 Manuel Dota - Ecuador
items.desc: Our first year working with Manuel Dota marks a continuation of our very small but compelling project in southern Ecuador. As always, the selection is very, very small, but we hope the size of these lots will grow with time. In the cup we find a classic Sidra profile of dragon fruit, eucalyptus, and stone fruit.

items.title: 2026 Héctor Londoño; Santa Catalina - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year working with Héctor's coffee. Part of our ongoing project to explore the Chiroso variety, this lot comes specifically from Urrao. In the cup we find a bright tropical profile with melon and soft florals.

items.title: 2026 Raro - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a continuation of our exploration of a new processing and separation protocol that we developed with our partners in Ethiopia this year. This lot was made with cherry from a site we used to work with years ago and has some of the highest-elevation coffee in Uraga. In the cup we find ripe stone fruit, very lively acidity, and rose hips.

items.title: 2026 Albino Ibias; Tres Cedros, 2nd Harvest - Peru
items.desc: The second harvest pass from Albino Ibias's farm arrives at an exciting moment—Tres Cedros is quickly gaining the reputation of producing some of the best coffee in Peru, and we are proud to continue working with this coffee. In the cup we find a clean tropical profile, with star fruit, peach, honeydew, and florals.

items.title: 2026 Felix Morocho; 2nd Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This is our second separation of the season from Felix Morocho. Felix is a newer producer to our Ecuador project, and this extremely small lot—like every other coffee we source from this region—is full of love and passion. In the cup we find peach, star fruit, and lemongrass.

items.title: 2026 Diana Arboleda Tabares; La Esperanza - Colombia
items.desc: Diana took over managing her father's small farm in 2011 and is a welcomed recent addition to our Chiroso project in Urrao. In the cup we find what we are starting to call a traditional Chiroso profile: tropical fruit, very bright acidity, with some florality.

items.title: 2026 Florence & Jessica Marigi; Malaki Estate - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first year working with Florence and Jessica. Their farm, Malaki, sits at very high elevation in Kiambu—one of the more intriguing coffee-producing regions in central Kenya. In the cup we find a dark fruit profile of blackcurrant, rhubarb, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Basha Bekele; Badigalo - Ethiopia
items.desc: Badigalo is Basha Bekele's new higher-elevation site, and this is our first year working with it. The quality has been exceptional. In the cup we find kiwi, orange blossom, and guava.

items.title: 2026 Mbature Family; Kamavindi Estate, Lot #1 - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first micro lot of the season from Kamavindi. Kamavindi is one of our main collaborators in Kenya, and the center of our ongoing exploration of Kenyan varieties and nano lot separations. In the cup we find rooibos, candied grapefruit, and blackcurrant.

items.title: 2026 David Berrio; La Casita, End Of Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is the last harvest pass from David Berrio's small garden of Chiroso. David had an exceptional year this year and his lots have been some of the highest scoring lots from Urrao we have tasted all year. In the cup we find ripe stone fruit, yellow florals, and star fruit.

items.title: 2026 Ndwiga Family; Nginda Estate - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first year working with the Ndwiga Family. Nginda Estate is a small family farm and a neighbor of our exporting partners, Kamavindi, who presented us with a sample of this delightful lot. In the cup we find red currant, rose hips, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Esayas Beriso; Buku Sayisa - Ethiopia
items.desc: We have been working with Esayas Beriso for a few seasons now, and the quality continues to be exceptional. This lot is one of the few single-producer separations we get from the Guji Highlands, and we are excited to be working with it again this season. In the cup we find peach rings, raspberry, and white tea.

items.title: 2026 Miguel Dota - Ecuador
items.desc: This is our second release from Miguel Dota, continuing our project in the Saraguro region of Ecuador. Grown in a small Sidra garden on a sub-1-hectare (~2.5-acre) farm, this lot is an exciting representation of the quality we now know can be found in this area. In the cup we find rose hips, hops, and ripe strawberries.

items.title: 2026 Siti - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first year working with this specific washing station located in Siti, which is a sub-kebele of Worka Chelbesa. The coffee from this region has been exceptional this season. In the cup we find watermelon, peach rings, white florals, and citrus.

items.title: 2026 Marta & Jose Florez; El Silencio - Colombia
items.desc: Marta and Jose are an inspiring young couple who grew up in the countryside of Antioquia. After marrying, they purchased a farm high up in Urrao and chose to focus on quality by planting one of our favorite varieties: Chiroso. In the cup we find a structured profile, excellent density, and notes of gooseberry, lychee, and chamomile.

items.title: 2026 Rolando Ramirez; El Mirador - Peru
items.desc: This is another special lot from the Santa Teresa region just outside of Cusco. This year marked our first real exploration of this area, and it opened our eyes to how special and diverse coffees from Peru can be. In the cup we find white florals, tea, and ripe stone fruit.

items.title: 2026 Magna Maldonado Padilla - Peru
items.desc: We have only sourced a handful of coffees from northern Peru. This is a compelling expression of the Gesha variety grown in a region we very rarely work in. In the cup we find apple blossom, cherry, and Key lime.

items.title: 2026 Anthony Kimani; Kibingo - Kenya
items.desc: The quality of Kibingo Estate last year was exceptional, and we were eager to see what this year's harvest would bring. It did not disappoint. Anthony has produced some of the top lots in Kenya, and it is an honor to again have the opportunity to work with his coffee. In the cup we find dark fruit, rose hips, and lemon.

items.title: 2026 Edid Medina - Peru
items.desc: This is our first year working with Edid Medina, an extremely dedicated producer and a leader within the San Fernando Cooperative. In the cup we find a fruit-forward profile of strawberry preserves, excellent sweetness, and softer acidity.

items.title: 2026 Gilber Huayllas; Llaqta Pata - Peru
items.desc: This is our first year working with Gilber Huayllas and his small SL9* garden at extremely high altitudes in the Amaybamba valley. In the cup we find violet, candied orange, and lemon.

items.title: 2026 Alo; Bombe - Ethiopia
items.desc: Coffees from Bombe are grown at extreme elevations nestled in the valleys of the Sidama mountains. This unique location consistently produces some of the highest-scoring coffees of the year. In the cup we find watermelon, white florals, and raspberry.

items.title: 2026 Luis & Mildred Montoya; La Arboleda - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year working with coffee from La Arboleda. This coffee was produced by Luis and his daughter, Mildred, and continues our exploration of Urrao. In the cup we find mulberry, peach, and lemon.

items.title: 2026 Georgina Puma; Monte Verde - Peru
items.desc: This is our first year working with Georgina and her extremely small garden of Gesha, tucked away in the mountains of Santa Ana in Cusco. In the cup we find apple blossom, mandarin, and blueberry.

items.title: 2026 Jhon Alexander Bermudez; Finca La Estrella, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is the second harvest pass from Jhon Alexander Bermudez’s garden of Chiroso. As one of the cornerstone producers in our Urrao project, Jhon Alexander continues to produce exceptional quality year after year. In the cup we find ripe pineapple, bright acidity, and hops.

items.title: 2026 Chelbessa - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first arrival of the season from the renowned Chelbessa site in Gedeb, Yirgacheffe. We have been working with Chelbessa for many years now, and its arrival on the menu is always a sign of summer. In the cup we find watermelon, peach, and citrus.

items.title: 2026 Boneya Robe; Chorso Bule - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a very special single-producer lot from Boneya Robe. He has a very small garden at an extreme altitude in Gedeb. Only the ripest cherries were selected, and the processing was meticulous. In the cup we find ripe peach, watermelon, and sweet tea.

items.title: 2026 William Ortiz; La Cabaña, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is the second harvest pass of William Ortiz’s Chiroso. His first harvest this year was quite literally one of the highest-scoring coffees we tasted from Colombia, and we are excited to share this new release. In the cup we find a softer yet complex tropical profile with melon and lime.

items.title: 2026 Pepe & Family; Finca Soledad, Sidra - Ecuador
items.desc: Pepe and his family live and breathe terroir. This beautiful expression of the Sidra variety reflects the regenerative, fully organic practices at Finca Soledad. In the cup we find eucalyptus honey, lemon tea, and white florals.

items.title: 2026 Pepe & Family; Finca Soledad, Mejorado - Ecuador
items.desc: Pepe is love, nature, and energy—all of which he pours into every lot of coffee he produces. This is another very small, regenerative, and organic selection from Pepe and his family, and each year it is an honor to work with these remarkable coffees. In the cup we find a sweet profile of fresh strawberries, hibiscus, and dulce de leche.

items.title: 2026 David Berrio; La Casita, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: David Berrio’s small garden produced the first Chiroso we truly fell in love with, and he continues to produce some of the highest-scoring Chiroso selections each year. This second harvest pass comes from the peak of the main harvest and is remarkably complex. In the cup we find a wildly tropical profile with ripe stone fruit and yellow florality.

items.title: 2026 Dwight Aguilar Masias; Finca Nueva Alianza, Red Gesha - Peru
items.desc: Over the last few years, Dwight has become one of the leading coffee producers in Peru, with multiple top placements in the Cup of Excellence. In this Red Gesha separation we find a floral-forward profile of jasmine, lychee, and honeydew.

items.title: 2026 Danche, Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is one of our longest-standing partnerships in Gedeb, Ethiopia. We have been working with the Danche site for many years, and this particular selection is a specific process developed in collaboration with our supply partners. In the cup we find watermelon, apricot, and lovely florality.

items.title: 2026 Carlos Saenz; Machay Pata - Peru
items.desc: This release continues our exploration of the SL9* variety from the remarkable region of Amaybamba. Coffees from this area have been extraordinary this season. In the cup we find mango, jasmine, and lychee.

items.title: 2026 Juan Danilo Florez; Las Mañanitas - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing coffee from Juan Florez, and a continuation of our exploration of Urrao and the Chiroso variety. In the cup we find yellow tropical fruit, soft florals, and hops.

items.title: 2026 Juan Jiménez; El Porvenir - Colombia
items.desc: We have been buying coffee from Juan Jiménez for years now, and he consistently produces some of the best Pink Bourbon in southern Huila. In the cup we find a bright, citrus-forward profile with apple blossom and lychee.

items.title: 2026 Gerald Njagi; Kambarare Special Preparation - Kenya
items.desc: Gerald prepared this single-bucket lot for us this year with the goal of perfectly uniform cherry selection. The result is a very big, fully tropical fruit-forward profile with an almost sticky sweetness and excellent acidity.

items.title: 2026 William Ortiz; La Cabaña, Aji - Colombia
items.desc: William Ortiz has produced some of our favorite coffees this season, and we are pleased to be working with this Aji separation for the first time. We have released only a handful of Aji lots over the years, and look forward to continuing this exploration. In the cup we find rose, açaí, and ripe raspberry.

items.title: 2026 Luis Salas; El Paraiso - Peru
items.desc: This is our second year purchasing Luis Salas's Gesha separation. Luis, and the incredible florality of his coffee, is the reason why we were first drawn to the Santa Teresa region and why we continued to explore it in more depth this season. We are honored to again have the opportunity to work with his coffee. In the cup we find yellow tropical fruit, white peach, and jasmine.

items.title: 2026 Chorso Bule - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first year working with the Chorso Bule site, which rests at some of the highest elevations in all of Gedeb. In the cup we find peach tea, melon, and jasmine.

items.title: 2026 Duber Mejia; El Diamante - Colombia
items.desc: This lot from Duber Mejia is easily one of the best coffees we have tasted from Urrao this year. The coffee is remarkably articulated and complex, and it is rare to encounter coffee of this caliber from a largely unknown producer. In the cup we find prickly pear, lychee, and honeydew.

items.title: 2026 Felix Morocho - Ecuador
items.desc: This is our first separation from Felix Morocho. As always, lots from this project are extremely small and full of love and passion. In the cup we find eucalyptus, nectarine, and white tea.

items.title: 2026 Jose & Pepe Jijón And Francisco Vintimilla; Putushio - Ecuador
items.desc: This stunning lot from the Jijóns and Francisco Vintimilla comes from one of the most unique microclimates we have encountered in coffee cultivation. Their remarkable farm sits atop a high-elevation bluff in an exceptionally dry landscape, yet remains sustained by a natural abundance of water. In the cup we find a nuanced and elegant profile of dragon fruit, honeydew, and rosewater.

items.title: 2026 Eduardo Quispe; Corral Pampa - Peru
items.desc: This is one of our first releases of the season from the incredibly special San Fernando Valley. We spent significant time in this valley this season, and our exploration here is just beginning. In the cup we find yellow tropical fruit, red grape, and honeydew.

items.title: 2026 Ibonia Estate; AB Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is our second year purchasing coffee from the renowned Ibonia Estate in Kiambu. Kenya remains something of a mystery as we try to track profiles around all the regions surrounding Mt. Kenya. Kiambu has traditionally been one of our favorites. This fun new selection tastes of hibiscus, blackcurrant, and rosehips.

items.title: 2026 Juan Zapata; La Guadua - Colombia
items.desc: Juan’s coffee is a continuation of our exploration of Urrao. This region and variety have become integral to our sourcing program, bringing an exceptionally articulated tropical profile to the current lineup. In the cup we find granadilla and lychee with subtle florality.

items.title: 2026 Arley Arboleda; Los Guaicos - Colombia
items.desc: We have been working on this project in Urrao for a number of years, but this is our first year purchasing coffee from Arley Arboleda. In the cup we find tropical fruit, lively acidity, and excellent structure.

items.title: 2026 Juan Pablo Ortiz; La Estella - Peru
items.desc: Juan Pablo has a very small garden of 100% Gesha, and is extremely dedicated to quality, gaining recognition in the international market, and showing the world the quality potential that exists in Vilcabamba. In the cup we find apple blossom, lychee, and honeydew.

items.title: 2026 José Peña; Los Naranjos - Colombia
items.desc: Our first coffee from José Peña continues our exploration of Urrao and the Chiroso variety. This region and variety continue to shift the conversation around quality and the diversity of flavor profiles within Colombian coffee, and we are excited to continue this exploration. In the cup we find yellow tropical fruit, candied strawberry, and hops.

items.title: 2026 Danche, White Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This year, we worked with the Danche site and the SNAP quality control team to try to build even higher-quality lot selections. The results of these new protocols have been exceptional. In the cup we find peach tea, watermelon, and Key lime.

items.title: 2026 Dwight Aguilar Masias; Yellow Gesha* - Peru
items.desc: Dwight Aguilar is a force in Peruvian coffee, with multiple placements in the Peru Cup of Excellence. He is widely considered to be the first to cultivate the mysterious Yellow Gesha* variety. This was our highest-scoring coffee during our last trip to Peru, and it is a special one. In the cup we find a floral-forward profile of jasmine and lilac, soft tropical fruit, and melon.

items.title: 2026 Karatu; AB Separation - Kenya
items.desc: Karatu has long been known for its quality in the Kiambu region of central Kenya, but this is our first year selecting a lot from this well-known site. In the cup we find rhubarb, hibiscus, and red currant.

items.title: 2026 Alberto Trujillo; La Estrella - Colombia
items.desc: This is a Pink Bourbon selection from a region we worked in more extensively in the past. Rica Brisa in Tarqui has always been a bit mysterious, and it is exciting to bring a lot from this special place back to the menu. In the cup we find raspberry jam, Key lime, and caramel apple.

items.title: 2026 Banko Gotiti - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first Ethiopian release of the season. We have been working with coffees from Banko Gotiti for several years now, and this is one of the best expressions we have tasted to date. In the cup we find peach tea, lemongrass, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2026 Edgardo Cruz Meza - Peru
items.desc: This is our first year working with Edgardo's coffee and one of the few selections we made from northern Peru in the region of Cajamarca. In the cup we find dragon fruit, Key lime, and jasmine.

items.title: 2026 Ayde Palomino Rojas; Flor Del Valle - Peru
items.desc: This release continues our exploration of the Santa Teresa region, which first captured our attention last season for its exceptional quality. This is our first year working with Ayde Palomino and her extremely small 1-hectare (~2.5-acre) garden of SL9*. In the cup we find orange blossom, honeydew, and mango.

items.title: 2026 Reynaldo Luque; Nueva Esperanza - Peru
items.desc: Amaybamba continues to be an exceptionally mysterious and captivating place. This is our first year working with Reynaldo Luque’s coffee, and we are excited to continue exploring this region. In the cup we find orange blossom, dragon fruit, and pineapple.

items.title: 2026 Marlene Rojas; El Nevado - Peru
items.desc: This is our second year purchasing coffee from Marlene Rojas. She produced one of our favorite Geshas from Peru last year, and we are excited to have her coffee again this season. In the cup we find ripe peach, white florals, and fresh blueberries.

items.title: 2026 Jhon Alexander Bermudez; Finca La Estrella - Colombia
items.desc: Jhon Alexander Bermudez’s Chiroso continues to show one of the most unique profiles we have found in Colombia, reminiscent of coffees from Uraga, Ethiopia. In the cup we find ripe pineapple, bright acidity, and hops.

items.title: 2026 Wilson Alba; Sierra Morena, End of Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is the final harvest pass of the season from Wilson Alba. His work with Pink Bourbon continues to inspire, and each opportunity to taste his coffee affirms just how special his approach is. In the cup we find berry compote, lemon zest, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Vicente Regalado; La Capilla - Ecuador
items.desc: We have been working on a project in Loja, Ecuador, for a few years now, and while the lots remain extremely small and limited, the quality has been exceptional. Vicente is a new producer to this project, and we are excited to be roasting his coffee. In the cup we find preserved lemon, orange blossom, and fresh herbs.

items.title: 2026 Juan Jose Huillca; Lot #Y-3 - Peru
items.desc: Yanatile is one of the most remarkable places we have visited. The mountains are breathtaking, and the energy is deeply inspiring. This is one of only a handful of lots we purchased from this special place. In the cup we find persimmon, orange blossom, and lilac.

items.title: 2026 William Ortiz; La Cabaña, Chiroso - Colombia
items.desc: Chiroso was, for many years, found only in Urrao—much farther north than Huila—but some southern producers have recently begun cultivating this unique variety. This is the second separation from William Ortiz and an exemplary expression of that effort. In the cup we find a stone fruit–forward profile of peach, lemon zest, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2026 Lisbeth Quispe; Yanacocha - Peru
items.desc: We have long been interested in coffees from the Sandia Valley in southern Peru, and this selection from Lisbeth Quispe marks the first lot we have been able to bring in from this valley. In the cup we find apricot, lychee, and Pink Lady apple.

items.title: 2026 Octavio Rueda; El Mirador, End Of Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is the last harvest pass of the season from the prolific and talented Octavio Rueda. It has been fascinating to observe how each pass has evolved throughout the season—this particular pass is the most intense and dynamic. In the cup we find blueberry, hibiscus, and pink lemonade.

items.title: 2026 Ninga; Bumba Hill, May 15th Harvest - Burundi
items.desc: This is our last release from Burundi this year. Burundi remains one of the most challenging origins we work in and produces some of the most unique profiles in coffee, so this selection is a fond farewell until next season. In the cup we find dried berries, spice, and orange marmalade.

items.title: 2026 Guchienda Estate; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: We have been working with Guchienda Estate for several years and are proud to continue working with this talented family. They have consistently produced some of the best Kenyan coffees, and we are grateful to Edwin, Benson, and their mother, Esther for continuing to work with us. In the cup we find ripe currants, rose hips, and tree tomato.

items.title: 2026 Victor Dota - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the first exportable harvest of the season from Victor Dota, and still one of the best representations of Mejorado from Ecuador. This lot comes from his tiny 0.5-hectare (1.2-acre) farm, which we are excited to see continue to mature. In the cup we find Key lime, floral botanicals, and ripe stone fruit.

items.title: 2026 Genezard Perez; Vista Alegre - Peru
items.desc: Genezard has an exceptionally beautiful farm situated alongside an enormous nature reserve in the San Fernando Valley. In the cup we find florals, prickly pear, and lychee.

items.title: 2026 David Berrio; Chiroso, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This lot marks the beginning of a new harvest season from Urrao. It is always exciting to receive an exceptionally fresh first-pass harvest from La Casita, the smallest Chiroso garden we work with. In the cup we find ripe tropical fruit, linden flower, with exceptional sweetness and structure.

items.title: 2026 Umoco; Busambo Hill - Burundi
items.desc: Our first year working with the Umoco washing station continues our exploration of Burundi. Coffees from this region hold a unique place in the landscape of coffee, and we have come to love these profiles over the years. Nowhere produces coffees quite like those found around Lake Kivu in northwestern Burundi. In the cup we find dark fruit leather, black tea, and baking spice.

items.title: 2026 Candelaria Santos; Tres De Mayo - Peru
items.desc: This is one of the few coffees we selected from northern Peru this season. It is also a rare opportunity for us to work with the Caturra variety again, which has played an important role in our sourcing from the very beginning. In the cup we find cherry, panela, and apple.

items.title: 2026 Ruarai; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first release from Kenya this season. This coffee comes from Nyeri on the western slopes of Mount Kenya—one of the most famous coffee-producing regions in the world. In the cup we find rose hips, pomegranate, and candied grapefruit.

items.title: 2026 Perlitas - Colombia
items.desc: This is the first lot of the main Chiroso harvest from Urrao this season. In the cup we find yellow tropical fruit, jam-like sweetness, and fresh hops.

items.title: 2026 Samuel & Mario Muriel; Los Cedros - Peru
items.desc: This release continues our exploration of the Inkawasi Valley and the SL9* variety. Samuel and Mario are inspired second-generation coffee producers with an exceptionally beautiful and steep farm at excellent elevation with remarkable biodiversity. In the cup we find a structured profile with tropical notes, subtle florality, and very high sweetness.

items.title: 2026 Servio Botina; El Cedro - Colombia
items.desc: Servio Botina produces some of our favorite coffees in all of southern Huila. We discovered his coffee several years ago and have never looked back. In the cup we find pomegranate, lime zest, and strawberry.

items.title: 2026 Ruvumu - Burundi
items.desc: This is our first year working with the Ruvumu washing station. We have always loved coffees from Burundi, and these profiles hold a special place for us. This marks the beginning of expanding our exploration of this remarkable coffee-producing country. In the cup we find blood orange, baking spice, and purple fruit.

items.title: 2026 Armando Hurtado; Los Pinos - Peru
items.desc: This is our second year purchasing coffee from Armando Hurtado. His coffee was one of the handful that opened our eyes to the incredible potential of this variety and this unique place and terroir. In the cup we find remarkable complexity with layers of tropical fruit and florality.

items.title: 2026 Diego Parra; La Hacienda, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is the second harvest pass from Diego Parra. Brother to Yessica Parra, this sibling project has produced some of the best lots of the season. In the cup we find candied lemon, red currant, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Wilbert Almanza; Bella Rosa - Peru
items.desc: We have known Wilbert for a number of years as the head of quality control and marketing for the San Fernando Cooperative. This is our first year working with his coffee, and this season’s lot is stunning. In the cup we find tropical fruit and lavender with incredible sweetness.

items.title: 2026 Samuel Aragon; Caminos Del Inka, Gesha - Peru
items.desc: This is a special coffee representing a new community we are focusing on in the Santa Teresa region. Samuel Aragon is a talented young producer growing excellent Gesha, and this was one of the most exciting coffees we tasted while in Peru. In the cup we find coffee blossom, mango, peach, and silver needle tea.

items.title: 2026 Jhon Saenz; Aromas De Aniz - Peru
items.desc: This lot comes from extreme elevations on the slopes of Mount Chogesafra, in the shadow of an immense nature reserve. In the cup we find ripe peach, dragon fruit, star fruit, and honeysuckle.

items.title: 2026 Bukeye; Musumba, Lot #1 - Burundi
items.desc: This is the only coffee we will release this year from the rolling hills of Musumba, where the rich soils and cool canopies of banana trees create ideal conditions for coffee cultivation. In the cup we find dried apricot, black tea, and blood orange.

items.title: 2026 Neto; La Margarita, Sidra Reserve Lot - Peru
items.desc: Neto is an incredibly inspired young producer who completely blew us away in Peru this year. We are genuinely excited for the opportunity to work with this exceptional coffee. In the cup we find blackcurrant, clementine, lemon zest, and soft ginger.

items.title: 2026 Neto; La Margarita, Yellow Gesha Reserve Lot - Peru
items.desc: Each year we meet many new and inspiring producers, but Neto stands out. After an introduction from Pepe Jijón, we visited his farm this fall—and were absolutely blown away. In the cup we find jasmine, blackberry, mandarin, and star fruit.

items.title: 2026 Wilson Alba; Sierra Morena, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is the second harvest pass from Wilson Alba this season. His work with Pink Bourbon continues to inspire, and each opportunity to taste his coffee affirms just how special his approach is. In the cup we find berry compote, lemon zest, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Mery Garcito; Finca La Bendición - Ecuador
items.desc: We have long loved coffees from the unique microclimate of La Papaya—an isolated, canyon-like environment that continues to produce some of the most compelling profiles in Ecuador. In the cup we find increased florality, fragrant lemongrass, and yellow fruit, all supported by excellent structure.

items.title: 2026 Ninga; Bumba Hill, May 5th Harvest - Burundi
items.desc: This is our second selection from Bumba Hill, processed at the Ninga washing station. This hill had an exceptional year, producing many of our top lots from Burundi this season. In the cup we find poached pear, baking spice, and Earl Grey tea.

items.title: 2026 Albino Ibias; Tres Cedros - Peru
items.desc: This is a stunning representation of this still mysterious variety. It is our first year working with the Ibias family, but we expect they will soon be recognized globally for the exceptional quality of their coffee. In the cup we find tropical melon, jasmine, honey, and peach.

items.title: 2026 Yessica Parra; El Mirador, Gesha - Colombia
items.desc: We have known Yessica for several years through her work in quality control. This is our first year buying her coffee, and it is exceptional. This selection is an excellent representation of Gesha, with very good density. In the cup we find white florals, ripe apricot, lemon verbena, and white sugar.

items.title: 2026 Ludivia Luna; El Diviso - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year working with Ludivia Luna’s coffee. We have released a number of Aruzi selections over the years, but it remains a variety we are still getting to know—and our exploration has only just begun. In the cup we find ripe plum, white grape, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Diego Parra; La Hacienda, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: Diego Parra is an exceptional producer, and this is an exquisite expression of Pink Bourbon from southern Huila. In the cup we find dark fruit, Key lime, and pomegranate.

items.title: 2026 Bukeye; Gaharo Hill - Burundi
items.desc: Gaharo Hill and the Bukeye washing station have been a cornerstone of our sourcing journey, consistently producing some of our favorite coffees from Burundi since the very beginning. In the cup we find gingerbread, baked apple, and honey.

items.title: 2026 Albeiro Ramirez; El Roble - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year working with Albeiro’s coffee. This is an excellent representation of this special variety and a unique expression, coming from farther south in Urrao. In the cup we find gooseberry, peach, and star fruit.

items.title: 2026 William Ortiz; La Cabaña, Pink Bourbon - Colombia
items.desc: William Ortiz is one of the more exciting producers we have met recently, and this Pink Bourbon separation marks our first season including his coffee in our Huila project. In the cup we find pink lemonade, strawberry preserve, and soft florals.

items.title: 2026 Alejandro Renjifo; Reina De Saba, Typica - Colombia
items.desc: 100% Typica is becoming increasingly rare in the world of high-end specialty coffee. This lot offers a unique opportunity to taste this important variety. In the cup we find a very clean and transparent expression of terroir: dark berries, honeysuckle, and lemon curd.

items.title: 2026 Alejandro Renjifo; Reina De Saba, Gesha - Colombia
items.desc: Each year we look forward to tasting the harvest from Reina de Saba. This Gesha consistently shows one of the more unique profiles for the variety, and this year's harvest is a standout expression. In the cup we find honeydew, lilac, and pomelo.

items.title: 2026 Ninga; Bumba Hill, April 28th Harvest - Burundi
items.desc: This is our first release from Burundi this year. For us, Bumba Hill produced the highest quality lots of the season. We decided to purchase several different harvest passes from this hill—this is the first. In the cup we find black tea, plum, and poached pear.

items.title: 2026 Miller Sarmiento; Lote Tres - Colombia
items.desc: This is a unique blend from a new producer—an uncommon combination of Sidra and Pink Bourbon. These varieties are typically separated, but the small size of each lot created an opportunity to do something different. In the cup we find strawberry jam, lemon zest, and panela.

items.title: 2026 Octavio Rueda; El Mirador, 4th Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is the fourth harvest pass from the prolific and talented Octavio Rueda—right at the peak of the season for this farm. It has been fascinating to observe how each pass has evolved throughout the season. In the cup we find blueberry, rose hips, and pink lemonade.

items.title: 2026 Kanzu; Lot #726 - Rwanda
items.desc: Coffees from around Lake Kivu in western Rwanda are special. This region produces some of the most distinct profiles in coffee, and for that reason, we love working with them. In the cup we find excellent density, plum, orange, and baking spices.

items.title: 2025 Jose & Pepe Jijón And Francisco Vintimilla; Putushio, Lots #37 & #42 - Ecuador
items.desc: This stunning lot from the Jijóns and Francisco Vintimilla comes from one of the most unique microclimates we have encountered in coffee cultivation. Their remarkable farm sits atop a high-elevation bluff in an exceptionally dry landscape, yet is sustained by a natural abundance of water. In the cup we find a nuanced and elegant profile of dragon fruit, honeydew, and rosewater.

items.title: 2025 Harmufo, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is the first time coffee from the high elevations around Harmufo has been separated as its own lot. We have been interested in this area for some time, and our exporting partner, SNAP, helped make this selection possible. In the cup we find lemon candy, ripe berries, and honeydew.

items.title: 2025 Jhonatan Pito; Dos Pinos - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year working with producer Jhonatan Pito. We discovered this coffee when its clarity and expression leapt off one of our buying tables. In the cup we find excellent structure, tangerine, honey, and blueberry.

items.title: 2025 Alberto & Carlos Lizarazo; El Brillante - Colombia
items.desc: This is a unique blend of Gesha and Pink Bourbon—two varieties that are almost always separated. It offers a rare opportunity to taste how these exceptional profiles interact. In the cup we find honeysuckle, Key lime, and strawberry.

items.title: 2025 William Ortiz; La Cabaña, Chiroso - Colombia
items.desc: Chiroso was, for many years, found only in Urrao—much farther north than Huila—but some southern producers have recently begun cultivating this unique variety. This separation from William Ortiz is an exemplary expression of that effort. In the cup we find a stone fruit–forward profile of peach, lemon zest, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2025 Pepe Jijón; Finca Soledad, New Season - Ecuador
items.desc: Pepe Jijón is love, nature, and energy—all of which he pours into every lot of coffee he produces. This is another very small, regenerative, and organic selection, and each year we are privileged to work with these remarkable coffees. In the cup we find tree tomato, black currant, and molasses.

items.title: 2025 Octavio Rueda; El Mirador, 3rd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This release continues our harvest separation project with Octavio Rueda, who has consistently produced one of our favorite profiles—one we are beginning to associate closely with the Pink Bourbon variety. This third harvest pass continues to impress. In the cup we find pomegranate, hibiscus, and limeade.

items.title: 2025 Benti Nenka - Ethiopia
items.desc: We have been purchasing coffee from this washing station under the watchful eye of Eyasu Worasa for several years now. This lot is exceptionally clean, with bergamot-like acidity, and notes of ripe peach, star fruit, and melon.

items.title: 2025 Victor Chala; La Palma Rosa - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first release from Victor Chala, an inspiring producer growing Pink Bourbon in southern Huila. We are excited to include his coffee in our selections this season, and look forward to visiting his farm on our next trip to Colombia. In the cup we find rose tea, orange zest, and elderberry.

items.title: 2025 Wilson Alba; Sierra Morena, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is the first harvest of the new season from Wilson Alba, a producer who has redefined the quality threshold for Pink Bourbon in recent years. His coffees have consistently dominated local competitions and reshaped our expectations for the variety and region. In the cup we find wild berries, limeade, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2025 Flor Marina Betancourt; Finca Cataluña - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first release from producer Flor Betancourt, and a continued exploration of the Pink Bourbon variety in Huila. In the cup we find lemon candy, strawberry, and oolong.

items.title: 2025 Crispilliano Contreras x Lost Origin - Panama
items.desc: The cherries for this special collaboration were harvested from Crispilliano’s extremely high-elevation Gesha garden and transported in refrigerated trucks to the Lost Origin lab in Panama City for highly controlled and intentional processing. In the cup we find Jolly Rancher, jasmine, candied orange, and green apple.

items.title: 2025 Francy Burbano; Buena Vista, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year working with producer Francy Burbano. We were introduced to her coffee by our exporting partners in Huila, and we are excited to be featuring this selection in our menu this season. In the cup we find lemonade, strawberry, and oolong tea.

items.title: 2025 Elora; Lot #156 - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our final release from the Elora project in Arbegona, and while we are sad to see this series come to a close, we are proud to share this last selection. In the cup we find peach rings, watermelon, and lemon zest.

items.title: 2025 Gildardo & Yolanda Lopez; El Calamar, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is the first harvest of the season from Gildardo and Yolanda Lopez. We have been working with their coffee for many years now, and each year we look forward to tasting through their lots. In the cup we find dark honey, strawberry, and lime zest.

items.title: 2025 Gerbota - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first release from the Gerbota site, high in the hills of Gedeo, Yirgacheffe. It is a very sweet and expressive representation of the profiles this region is known for. In the cup we find nectarine, bergamot, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2025 Jair Arles Galindez; El Guayabo, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: It is an honor to continue working with coffee from this incredible and inspiring producer. Arles Galindez consistently delivers clean, articulate representations of each new season. In the cup we find lemon zest, fresh blueberries, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2025 Maritza Dota, Late - Ecuador
items.desc: This small release comes from Maritza’s garden of Mejorado in southern Loja, Ecuador. The Dota family has been producing exceptional coffees over the past year, and this lot is no exception. In the cup we find a lovely floral profile with sweet grapefruit, cane sugar, and lychee.

items.title: 2025 Yaye Chericho - Ethiopia
items.desc: Yaye Chericho is our second release of the season from Arbegona, a region that has consistently produced some of our highest-scoring lots in Ethiopia. This late-harvest selection was one of our last to land—and it was worth the wait. In the cup we find florals, peach, and complex melons.

items.title: 2025 Koko; Lot #159, Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first year working with the Koko site in the Bona region of Sidama. All the cherry for this lot was collected from extremely high elevations and carefully curated by our exporting partners at Elto. In the cup we find stone fruit, Key lime, and watermelon.

items.title: 2025 Eduar Moriones Garcia; Finca Brisa - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year tasting and purchasing coffee from Eduar Moriones Garcia. It is always exciting to work with a coffee for the first time—especially from Huila. In the cup we find ripe red fruit, lemon zest, and excellent structure.

items.title: 2025 Tamiru Tadesse Tesema; Alo Village, White Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a special honey process that Tamiru produced for us this year. We love honey-processed coffees from Bensa, and it is incredibly exciting to have this selection from Alo. In the cup we find dragon fruit, lychee, and berries.

items.title: 2025 Tamiru Tadesse Tesema; Alo Village, Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first year releasing Tamiru’s Classic Washed profile. Made from 100% 74158 variety, the cherry was selected from trees growing above 2,400 masl. Tamiru is one of the leading producers and voices in Ethiopian coffee, and it is an honor to be working with his coffee once again. In the cup we find ripe tropical fruit like guava, purple florals, and excellent acidity and complexity.

items.title: 2025 La Familia Moreno; La Sierra - Honduras
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing the Gesha separation from this farm, where we originally sourced coffee nearly a decade ago. In the cup we find soft florals, Key lime, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2025 Finca Sophia; Lots FS9025 & FS9325 - Panama
items.desc: Every year we wait anxiously to receive our lot allocations from Finca Sophia. This farm—and the coffee it produces—is, in a word, exceptional. In the cup we find articulated florality, ripe tropical fruit, and exceptional structure with deep complexity.

items.title: 2025 Duwancho - Ethiopia
items.desc: Duwancho has produced some of our highest-scoring Ethiopian lots from Arbegona. Long overshadowed by the more recognized region of Bensa, Arbegona has emerged in recent years as a source of some of the finest coffees in the world. In the cup we find watermelon, honeydew, and jasmine.

items.title: 2025 David Berrio; La Casita, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This marks the beginning of a new harvest season from Urrao. It is always exciting to receive an exceptionally fresh first-pass harvest from La Casita, the smallest Chiroso garden we work with. In the cup we find ripe tropical fruit, white tea, and exceptional sweetness and structure.

items.title: 2025 Octavio Rueda; El Mirador, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is the second harvest pass from Octavio Rueda, who has been producing some of the highest-scoring Pink Bourbon in Huila for several years. We hold both this coffee and producer in the highest regard. In the cup we find pomegranate, hibiscus, and lime.

items.title: 2025 Arturo Paz; El Itacayo - Honduras
items.desc: This is our first release from Arturo Paz, though we have known him for many years. Arturo is a remarkable coffee producer and also serves as the head of quality control at San Vicente, our longtime exporting partner. In the cup we find a classic Gesha profile of jasmine, peach, and white tea.

items.title: 2025 Miguel Dota - Ecuador
items.desc: This second release from Miguel Dota continues our new project in the Seraguro region of Ecuador. Grown in a small Sidra garden on a sub-1-hectare (~2.5-acre) farm, it showcases the expressive profiles we are beginning to expect from this special group of producers and region. In the cup we find matcha, mango, and ripe strawberries.

items.title: 2025 Elora; Lot #151, Fermented Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our final release from this season’s new project with the Elora site, and we could not be happier with how it has gone. These coffees have been stunning. In the cup, we find honeydew, papaya, and lime.

items.title: 2025 Yaye Arbegona - Ethiopia
items.desc: Yaye is one of the highest-elevation washing stations in the world and consistently produces some of our favorite profiles in all of coffee. Each year we look forward to this release. In the cup we find watermelon, lychee, and complex botanicals.

items.title: 2025 Paxtle - Mexico
items.desc: This regional blend from the Sierra Mazateca is composed of the highest-scoring lots that were too small to export individually. It comes from a producing group called Paxtle, based in San Mateo on the western side of the valley. In the cup we find a classic Mexican profile of baking chocolate, fresh strawberry, and honey.

items.title: 2025 Elora; Lot #25, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot comes from an exciting new project in one of our favorite coffee-growing regions, Arbegona. This beautiful honey-processed coffee is a striking example of the fruit complexity and florality this special region can produce. In the cup we find peach tea, hibiscus, apricot, and lime.

items.title: 2025 José Gallardo; Nuguo, Lot #850NWS - Panama
items.desc: This year we had the privilege of traveling to Finca Nuguo with José Gallardo to select this extremely small 15kg lot—an experience that challenged our ideas of what coffee can be. In the cup we find an intensely floral profile of jasmine and rose, Meyer lemon, and bergamot, with a slightly tropical finish.

items.title: 2025 Octavio Rueda; El Mirador, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: Octavio Rueda produces some of our favorite Pink Bourbon in all of Colombia. We have worked with this selection from El Mirador for several years now, and it remains a highlight each season. In the cup we find mango, strawberry, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2025 Esayas Beriso; Buku Sayisa - Ethiopia
items.desc: This vibrant coffee comes from extreme elevations in the Guji Highlands. A lively, single-estate selection, it offers a bright and expressive profile of sweet peach tea, ripe raspberry, and nectarine.

items.title: 2025 Digna Nuñez x Lost Origin - Panama
items.desc: We love the opportunity to work with lesser-known producers growing exceptional coffee—especially in Panama, where the landscape is often dominated by large estates and well-known names. Dinga is a school teacher in a small town outside Volcán, cultivating a tiny backyard garden of Gesha. In the cup we find white florality, lychee, and nectarine.

items.title: 2025 Elora; Galana, Lot #157 - Ethiopia
items.desc: This first release from our new project in Arbegona, Sidama, comes from the Elora site and is everything we hoped for. In the cup we find excellent density and structure, peach rings, lemonade, and tea.

items.title: 2025 Hamasho; Songo, Lot #154 - Ethiopia
items.desc: Hamasho has long produced some of the highest-scoring coffees in the world. This exploratory honey process lot was made possible through the dedication of the contributing producers and our exporting partner, Elto, to whom we are deeply grateful. In the cup we find ripe blueberry, peach tea, and lychee.

items.title: 2025 Jose & Pepe Jijón And Francisco Vintimilla; Finca San Pedro, Lot #30 - Ecuador
items.desc: This is a stunning lot from Pepe and Francisco, produced in one of the most unique microclimates we have seen in coffee cultivation. Their incredible farm sits on a high-elevation bluff in a dry climate, yet benefits from a natural abundance of water. In the cup we find a nuanced and elegant profile of dragon fruit, honeydew, and rose water.

items.title: 2025 Halo Hartume, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This year we worked with one of our favorite washing stations in Gedeb, Halo Hartume, to create a special white honey-processed lot for the first time. We could not be happier with the results. In the cup we find yellow peach, berries, honeysuckle, and lemon.

items.title: 2025 Anthony Kimani; Kibingo, AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This was our highest-scoring Kenyan selection of the year—and it also won Kenya’s Taste of Harvest competition. In the cup we find blackberry, plum, starfruit, and rose.

items.title: 2025 Gerald Njagi; Kambarare - PB Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This exceptionally small lot of Peaberry SL28 from Gerald’s farm, Kambarare, produced one of the highest-scoring Kenyan coffees in recent memory. Its profile differs slightly from the AA/AB separation. In the cup we find a more tropical and complex profile of mango, lychee, blackcurrant, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2025 Estela Pitti; Los Cenizos - Panama
notes: A very floral profile of jasmine
items.desc: This is our second year buying coffee from Estela, and this honey-processed lot was made exclusively for us. Los Cenizos, located beyond Volcán, produces some of the highest-elevation Gesha in Panama. In the cup we find a very floral profile of jasmine, neroli, nectarine, and lemon.

items.title: 2025 Bishan Wate - Ethiopia
items.desc: Our first year working with the Bishan Wate site in Hambela, Guji brought an unexpected standout on our buying tables this season. In the cup we find ripe berries, white peach, and lemon zest.

items.title: 2025 Franci Marin Morales; La Montañita - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing coffee from Fanci Morales, an exceptional producer who has consistently placed in regional competitions. She grows Pink Bourbon on a small 2-hectare (~4.9-acre) garden with remarkable care and precision. In the cup we find ripe forest berries, wildflower honey, and tea.

items.title: 2025 Jose Martinez; El Casino Gesha, End Of Season - Colombia
items.desc: We have worked with Jose Martinez for many years, but this is our first year purchasing his Gesha variety. It is a strong representation of what Gesha can be in the terroir of southern Huila. In the cup we find nectarine, white florals, and apricot.

items.title: 2025 Getachew Zeleke; Tero Farm - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first year working with coffee from Getachew Zeleke. While we have long loved the profiles from Guji, they have become increasingly difficult to find in recent years. Our hats are off to Getachew for producing this stunning coffee. In the cup we find white peach, jasmine, and pomelo.

items.title: 2025 Guchienda Estate; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: We have been working with the Guchienda Estate for several years, and it continues to produce some of the best Kenyan profiles we taste each season. This year is no different—our hats are off to Edwin, Benson, and their mother, Esther. In the cup we find ripe blackberry, hibiscus, and tree tomato.

items.title: 2025 Halo Hartume, Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: This year’s selection stays on the bright, crisp, and clean side of the profiles we see from Gedeb—offering a plethora of light fruit tones complemented by soft floral tea notes. The fruit character hovers between ripe peach, tropical nuance, and other stone fruits.

items.title: 2025 Maritza Dota, Late Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This second release from Maritza Dota continues our new project in the Seraguro region of Ecuador. Grown on a tiny 0.5-hectare (~1.2-acre) farm, this lot is a standout representation of the quality we are finding in this area. In the cup we find mandarin, floral botanicals, and ripe stone fruit.

items.title: 2025 Banko Gotiti - Ethiopia
items.desc: We have been working in Banko Gotiti for several years, and continue to love the cleanliness, brightness, and elegance of the coffees produced at this washing station. In the cup we find wildflower honey, tangerine, and apricot.

items.title: 2025 Jose Martinez; El Casino, End of Season - Colombia
items.desc: one of our most consistent quality-focused producers in southern Huila. In the cup we find red fruit, lemon zest, and fresh blueberry.

items.title: 2025 Florcita, Jose, & Pepe Jijón; Finca Soledad, 2nd Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This is a beautiful expression of the Sidra variety and a clear reflection of the regenerative, fully organic practices at Finca Soledad. In the cup we find melon, soft florals, and lime zest.

items.title: 2025 Pepe Jijón; Finca Soledad, TyOxy, 2nd Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the second TyOxy lot Pepe specially prepared for us this season, and it is another stunning work of art. We are not sure how he has maintained such consistently high quality this year, but it is truly remarkable. This is another very small, regenerative, and organic 30kg lot. In the cup we find blackberry juice with hints of tree tomato.

items.title: 2025 Victor Alfonso Bonilla; La Chorrera, End of Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is a fascinating coffee from a producer and variety we had never worked with until this year. Locally referred to as Aruzi, we suspect it is another Ethiopian Landrace being cultivated in Colombia. In the cup we find chamomile, honeydew, and peach.

items.title: 2025 David Berrio; La Casita, End of Season - Colombia
items.desc: We have now worked with several harvests from David Berrio’s garden, La Casita, and his small-scale, intentional approach continues to inspire. This third and final harvest pass is the most expressive of his Chiroso lots this season. In the cup we find a tropical-forward profile with vibrant acidity and clarity.

items.title: 2025 Servio Botina; El Cedro, End Of Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is the final harvest pass from producer Servio Botina, capping off another inspired year from this talented young grower. In the cup we find wild strawberry, crisp botanicals, and mandarin.

items.title: 2025 Kedida Gubata - Ethiopia
items.desc: Kedida Gubata is a new high-elevation separation from our export partners at SNAP. We have not released a coffee from Kochere in some time, but this lot is special. In the cup we find honeydew, nectarine, and lime.

items.title: 2025 Ernedis Rodriguez; El Paraiso, Lot #2 - Colombia
items.desc: Ernedis presented two distinct Caturra lots this year, and after extensive tasting, we found them uniquely different enough to keep fully separated. In the cup we find red fruit, yellow plum, and Key lime.

items.title: 2025 Muhito - Kenya
items.desc: Muhito is one of several washing station co-ops that participated in our SL variety separation project this year. In the cup we find a lovely traditional Kenyan profile of pomegranate, hibiscus, and rose.

items.title: 2025 José Jijón; Finca San Pedro, 4th Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the season’s fourth and final harvest pass from José Jijón’s new farm, Finca San Pedro. Located at some of the highest elevations we have seen for coffee in Ecuador, San Pedro is one of the most beautiful organic farms we have visited. In the cup we find prickly pear, honeydew, and rose.

items.title: 2025 Marta & Jose Florez; El Silencio - Colombia
items.desc: Marta and Jose are an inspiring young couple who grew up in the countryside of Antioquia. After marrying, they purchased a farm high up in Urrao and chose to focus on quality by planting one of our favorite varieties: Chiroso. In the cup we find a structured profile, excellent density, and notes of gooseberry and lemongrass.

items.title: 2025 Wilmer & Yenni Moncayo; La Loma - Colombia
items.desc: We have been working with these two young producers for a few years now, and both their story and their coffee continue to inspire. Their lots are consistently exceptional, and they are a pleasure to work with. In the cup we find a complex profile of tropical fruit, floral oolong, and berry-like sweetness.

items.title: 2025 Danche - Ethiopia
items.desc: Danche is located just a few kilometers from the famed Chelbessa washing station and consistently produces immaculate coffees year after year. In the cup we find Earl Grey tea, watermelon, peach, and lively citrus acidity.

items.title: 2025 Daniel Caro Lopez; El Tambo - Colombia
items.desc: This is another strong expression of Chiroso from the Caro family in Anzá. Daniel is an inspired young producer, and it is an honor to roast his coffee again this season. In the cup we find a yellow tropical profile with tamarind and rose.

items.title: 2025 Gerald Njagi; Kambarare - Kenya
items.desc: This year marks a special milestone in our ongoing work with Gerald and Kambarare. This lot, part of a project we are calling Retro 1984, is a 100% pure SL separation and a stunning expression of variety and place. In the cup we find pomegranate, black currant, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2025 Sike Bokossa - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first year working with coffee from the Sike Bokossa site. This selection marks the first time coffee from this site has been separated and exported as an individual lot. In the cup we find watermelon, peach, and lemongrass.

items.title: 2025 Jair Arles Galindez; El Guayabo, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: We look forward to tasting coffee from Jair every year. His Pink Bourbon is always loud, dynamic, and expressive. In the cup we find pomegranate, Meyer lemon, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2025 Bochessa - Ethiopia
items.desc: Our first selection from the community of Bochessa comes from the highlands of Sidama, in one of our favorite regions in Ethiopia: Arbegona. In the cup we find a peach-forward profile with lemon verbena and white tea.

items.title: 2025 Liliana Burbano; El Nogal, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: Our first selection from Liliana Burbano continues our exploration of Pink Bourbon from San Agustín. In the cup we find clementine, star fruit, and blueberry compote.

items.title: 2025 Julio Arotaype; Sol Naciente - Peru
items.desc: This is our second year working with SL9 from Julio Arotaype. Grown at the highest elevation of any farm we work with in Central and South America, this coffee delivers exceptional complexity. In the cup we find aromatic florality, layered stone fruit, and melon.

items.title: 2025 José Jijón; Finca San Pedro, 3rd Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the season’s third harvest pass from José Jijón’s new farm, Finca San Pedro. Located at some of the highest elevations we have seen for coffee in Ecuador, San Pedro is one of the most beautiful organic farms we have visited. In the cup we find pear, yellow melon, rose, and raspberry.

items.title: 2025 Juan Contreras; Layampata - Peru
items.desc: Juan Contreras produced one of the best SL9 lots we cupped this year. His farm sits just below an old-growth nature reserve high in the San Fernando Valley, and is fully organic. In the cup we find ripe nectarine, lychee, and jasmine pearls.

items.title: 2025 Ernedis Rodriguez; El Paraiso, 3rd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is a very exciting release, as we rarely have the opportunity to work with Caturra anymore. We are deeply grateful to Ernedis for producing this lot. In the cup we find dark fruit, citrus, and botanicals.

items.title: 2025 Nemesio Ramos; Las Galaxias, Copa de Oro - Colombia
items.desc: Caturra was one of our favorite varieties over a decade ago, but it has become increasingly difficult to find. We were glad to discover this exciting lot through this year’s Copa de Oro competition. In the cup we find green papaya, pomegranate, and citrus.

items.title: 2025 Mariela Muñoz; El Nacedero, Copa de Oro - Colombia
items.desc: We are excited to introduce Mariela Muñoz, a new producer to our lineup whose coffee placed 4th in this year’s Copa de Oro. This is our first year working with her, and we are honored to showcase her work. In the cup we find pronounced sweetness with notes of strawberry preserves, raspberry, and lime zest.

items.title: 2025 Abelardo Medina; El Girasol, Copa de Oro - Colombia
items.desc: Abelardo has quickly become one of our favorite producers in Huila. This is his Copa de Oro competition lot, and the final harvest we will see from his farm this season. In the cup we find white lilac, hibiscus, and tamarillo.

items.title: 2025 Gildardo Lopez; El Calamar, Copa de Oro - Colombia
items.desc: This is Gildardo Lopez’s Copa de Oro competition lot, and we were fortunate to secure a very small amount of this special selection. In the cup we find an intense and complex profile of blackberry lemonade, coffee blossom florals, and ripe nectarine.

items.title: 2025 Kayu; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: Our first coffee from Kayu offers a very cool look at Kenyan terroir beyond the slopes of Mount Kenya. Grown off the Aberdare Ridge in Murang’a County, this lot showcases a distinct regional profile. In the cup we find blackcurrant, hibiscus, and Key lime.

items.title: 2025 Mbature Family; Kamavindi Estate, Gesha - Kenya
