items.desc: We have tasted the Gesha from this farm since it was first planted. The trees are still young, but this is the second year there has been enough to roast and share. As expected, the quality continues to improve as the plants mature. This year, the cup is even more floral, with jasmine, peach nectar, and melon.

items.title: 2025 Eduardo Quispe; Corral Pampa - Peru
items.desc: Eduardo Quispe’s farm sits at an impressive elevation and is cultivated using fully organic, traditional growing practices. Though only five years old, it is already producing exceptional quality. In the cup we find mandarin orange, star fruit, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2025 David Berrio; La Casita, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: We have now worked with several harvests from David Berrio’s garden, La Casita, and his small-scale, intentional approach continues to inspire. This second pass is more refined than the first, with cleaner fruit expression and more articulated acidity. In the cup we find a tropical-forward profile with vibrant clarity.

items.title: 2025 Pepe Jijon; Finca Soledad, TyOxy - Ecuador
items.desc: A few years ago, Pepe sent us a sample of his TyOxy-processed Mejorado that we still refer to as lightning in a bottle. It was unlike anything we had tasted before. This season's extremely small 63kg lot is remarkably reminiscent of that first experience. In the cup we find an incredibly complex profile of dark berries, currants, and hibiscus, with a finish that seems to go on forever.

items.title: 2025 Marlene Rojas; El Nevado - Peru
items.desc: Peru—specifically the Cusco region—is one of the most exciting emerging coffee-producing areas. Marlene’s farm sits at one of the highest altitudes we have seen in South America, with unique varieties and genetics that contribute to outstanding quality. In the cup we find ripe nectarine, wildflowers, blueberry, and honey.

items.title: 2025 Kubi, Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: This selection comes from a small regional group of producers delivering to the Chelbessa washing station, which consistently produces some of our favorite Ethiopian coffees. In the cup we find intoxicating florals, watermelon, peach, and lively citrus acidity.

items.title: 2025 Octavio Rueda; El Mirador, 3rd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: Octavio has produced some of the highest-scoring Pink Bourbon we have tasted from Colombia. His coffees are consistently expressive, with remarkable intensity and complexity. In the cup we find tropical fruit, mango, pomegranate, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2025 Ericson Luque; Nueva Esperanza - Peru
items.desc: Ericson is a young producer and the son of Lucio Luque, whose coffee we are fortunate to also work with. His small garden of SL9 benefits from excellent genetics, terroir, and tradition, setting a strong foundation for quality. In the cup we find orange blossom, lychee, and red berries.

items.title: 2025 Isidro Orosco; Soqoy Qara - Peru
items.desc: Isidro Orosco is a new producer whose coffee we discovered during our visit to Peru last fall. His young organic farm is another example of how Peru is shaping the future landscape of coffee. In the cup we find coffee blossom, raspberry jam, and apricot.

items.title: 2025 Mbature Family; Kamavindi Estate, SL34 - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first fully traceable, single-producer SL34 separation from Kenya—a project made possible through years of commitment and close collaboration with the Mbature family. The effort to bring this lot to market reflects our dedication to showcasing the finest expressions of both Kenyan coffee and this variety. In the cup we find a very complex profile of yellow plum, pomegranate, and honeysuckle.

items.title: 2025 Mbature Family; Kamavindi Estate, SL28 - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first time working with a fully traceable, single-producer SL28 separation from Kenya. This project has been in the works for some time, but it truly came together during our last trip, sharing a meal with the Mbature family. This lot captures everything we seek in both Kenyan coffee and SL28. In the cup, we find blackberry, rooibos, and candied grapefruit.

items.title: 2025 Ricardo Silva; Finca El Suspiro - New Season, 1st Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: Ricardo remains the only producer we work with in Algeciras, Huila. While we have purchased his Gesha in the past, this year we selected a Pink Bourbon separation. In the cup we find softer stone fruits, plum, hibiscus, and rosewater.

items.title: 2025 Ernedis Rodriguez; El Paraiso - 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: We have worked with the Sidra from El Paraiso for years, watching the trees mature and the quality evolve. This lot is the finest Ernedis Rodriguez has produced yet. In the cup we find raspberries, eucalyptus, and peach.

items.title: 2025 Victor Alfonso Bonilla; La Chorrera - Colombia
items.desc: This is a fascinating coffee from a producer and variety we have never worked with before. Locally referred to as Aruzi, we suspect it is another Ethiopian Landrace variety being cultivated in Colombia. In the cup we find lemon verbena, yellow watermelon, and peach.

items.title: 2025 Carlos Saenz; Chirimoyayoc - Peru
items.desc: This is another selection from our new project in Cusco, Peru. With its extreme elevations and unique varieties, this region continues to reveal its immense potential. In the cup we find ripe melon, Key lime, and white florals.

items.title: 2025 Luis Salas; El Paraiso - Peru
items.desc: Luis is another young farm and producer from southern Peru. Rather than SL9 or ‘Inca Gesha,’ Luis Salas is cultivating Gesha with seeds sourced from Panama. Grown organically at extreme elevation in the heart of the Andes, this lot is a remarkable expression of the variety. In the cup we find lychee, apricot, delicate florals, and sparkling acidity.

items.title: 2025 Jair Arles Galindez; El Guayabo - Colombia
items.desc: We look forward to tasting coffee from Jair every year. His Pink Bourbon is consistently loud, dynamic, and expressive. In the cup we find strawberry lemonade, blueberry, and lemon candy.

items.title: 2025 Yesica Moreno; Finca El Rosal, Bourbon Chiroso - New Season, 1st Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is our second year sourcing a 100% Bourbon Chiroso separation from Yesica. Tasting this lot next to her Chiroso separation continues to be a fascinating experience. In the cup we find the tropical flavors we associate with Chiroso, along with more pronounced stone fruit and florality.

items.title: 2025 Yesica Moreno; Finca El Rosal, Chiroso - New Season, 1st Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is our second year working with Yesica Moreno’s coffees, and her Chiroso continues to be one of the most dynamic we taste each season. In the cup we find an intense and layered profile of tropical fruit, ripe strawberry, and delicate florals.

items.title: 2025 Armando Hurtado; Los Pinos - Peru
items.desc: Armando is another new and young producer whose coffee we tasted during our last trip to Cusco. Los Pinos is one of the most beautiful and diverse farms we have seen, a reflection of the complexity and quality of the coffee itself. In the cup we find vibrant layered fruit, sparkling acidity, and pronounced florality.

items.title: 2025 Rene Arellanos Ore; Garancalqui - Peru
items.desc: This is a fascinating coffee and a rare variety, colloquially known as ‘Typica Americana’. Its distinctive profile caught our attention immediately. In the cup we find a jam-like sweetness, apricot, and an almost salted plum quality.

items.title: 2025 Mbature Family; Kamavindi Estate, Field Blend - Kenya
items.desc: This single-estate selection comes from the Mbature family on the southeastern slopes of Mt. Kenya in Embu County. Working with their coffee is an honor—their dedication to quality is truly inspiring. In the cup we find dark fruits, pink grapefruit, and a rich, jam-like sweetness.

items.title: 2025 Lucio Luque - Peru
items.desc: This is an exceptional expression of the unique SL9 variety. Coffee cultivation in Peru continues to excite, and this specific variety is a standout. Lucio Luque is an inspired producer, and this selection truly shines. In the cup we find Gesha-like florality, limeade, and white grape.

items.title: 2025 Jose Martinez; El Casino, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: Jose Martinez has been one of the most consistent producers in southern Huila. His coffees are always expressive, and we look forward to them each harvest cycle. In the cup we find red tea, Key lime, and strawberry preserves.

items.title: 2025 Anibal Sanchez Burbano; La Siria - Colombia
items.desc: This outstanding Gesha separation comes from producer Anibal Sanchez, who earned 2nd place in the 2021 Cup of Excellence with this coffee. It is a beautifully floral example of what Gesha can be. In the cup we find heady white florals, ripe nectarine, and an exceptionally clean, expressive profile.

items.title: 2025 Oliva Quinayas; Villa Sofia - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing a lot from Oliva. It is a lovely expression of Pink Bourbon grown in San Agustín, and we look forward to visiting Villa Sofia next season. In the cup we find dark berries, molasses, and a long, complex finish.

items.title: 2025 Juan Jiménez; El Porvenir, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is the season’s first harvest pass from El Porvenir, and Juan Jiménez’s coffee continues to impress. In the cup, we find Key lime, lilac, and lychee.

items.title: 2025 Bukeye; Musumba Hill - Burundi
items.desc: This separation comes from the rolling hills of Musumba, where the rich soils and cool canopies of banana trees create ideal conditions for coffee cultivation. Despite its challenges, this region continues to show exceptional potential. In the cup we find red tea, currant, and clove.

items.title: 2025 Victor Dota - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the first exportable harvest from new producer Victor Dota and one of the best representations of Mejorado from Ecuador we tasted this year. This lot comes from a tiny .5-hectare (1.2-acre) farm, and we are excited to see it mature. In the cup we find Key lime, floral botanicals, and ripe stone fruit.

items.title: 2025 Lubier Beltran; Finca Tijuana - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing coffee from this young farm and family. Now in its fourth year of production, the quality is already exceptional. In the cup we find blood orange, raspberry, and lemon balm.

items.title: 2025 Olvin Moreno; Pinares - Honduras
items.desc: This extremely small farm, Pinares, has always been one of our favorites in all of Santa Bárbara. We are honored to offer this as a separated lot. In the cup we find a ripe and fresh expression of blueberries, hibiscus, bright acidity, and a long finish.

items.title: 2025 The Lamastus Family; Elida Estate, Gesha - Panama
items.desc: Gesha is a truly special variety; especially from Panama, and especially from this farm. Its flavors are defined, articulated, unique and elegant. This cup brings intoxicating florals of jasmine and honeysuckle together with a crisp citrus acidity and ripe stone fruit notes in a beautifully integrated experience.

items.title: 2025 Hector Hernandez; La Cumbre - Colombia
items.desc: This is a really cool Gesha from a new producer. Discovering new coffees and building relationships with new producers each year keeps this industry vibrant and makes our work endlessly exciting. In the cup we find jasmine, mango, and champagne.

items.title: 2025 Wilson Alba; Sierra Morena, 3rd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This lot comes from the third harvest pass at Sierra Morena this season. It is bright, crisp, and sweet, with pointed lemonade-like acidity, red currant, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2025 Ninga; Giku Hill - Burundi
items.desc: Giku’s remote location on the fringes of the Kibira Forest makes it one of the most isolated coffee-producing regions we work with. Despite the challenges, this unique environment yields truly exceptional coffee. In the cup we find a structured profile of stewed fruit, black tea, and warm baking spices.

items.title: 2025 Jose Jijon; Finca San Pedro, 2nd Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the season's second harvest pass from José Jijón’s new farm, Finca San Pedro. José is an inspired young coffee producer, and we are excited to see what the future holds for him. Located at some of the highest elevations we have seen for coffee production in Ecuador, San Pedro is one of the most beautiful farms we have ever visited. In the cup we find clean tropical fruit, rose, and raspberry.

items.title: 2025 Maritza Dota - Ecuador
items.desc: This is our first year working with Maritza Dota. Some of our favorite coffee profiles come from this unique variety grown in this remarkable country. In the cup we find orange blossom, ripe peach, and raspberry.

items.title: 2025 Fabian Munoz; El Deviso - Colombia
items.desc: Fabian Munoz is a new producer to our project in southern Huila. As much as we try to purchase coffee from the same producers year after year, it is always exciting to discover new producers each season. In the cup we find ripe strawberry, pink grapefruit, and rose hips.

items.title: 2025 Octavio Rueda; El Mirador - Colombia
items.desc: Octavio has produced some of our highest-scoring Pink Bourbon from Colombia. His coffees are consistently expressive, with remarkable intensity and complexity. In the cup we find pink lemonade, pomegranate, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2025 Oscar Hernan Garcia; San Isidro - Colombia
items.desc: This is a new Gesha separation from producer Oscar Garcia, and our first year purchasing this lot. In the cup we find a fruit-forward expression of the Gesha variety, with notes of lychee, pomegranate, and jasmine.

items.title: 2024 Abel Salinas; Arashi - Ecuador
items.desc: This is a beautifully transparent and clean representation of Mejorado, sourced from Loja in southern Ecuador. The profile is elegant and refined, with layers of soft florals, peach, and lemon.

items.title: 2024 Ticuna; El Esquilino, SL28 - Colombia
items.desc: This is the third harvest from José and Kyle’s extraordinary project, and it has been fascinating to witness how these profiles are evolving as the trees mature. In the cup we find subtle yellow tropicals, berry-like complexity, and a white peach florality.

items.title: 2024 Familia Vallecillo; Los Primos, Yellow Pacas - Honduras
items.desc: Yellow Pacas is a regressive trait within the Pacas variety, making it especially unique to taste this 100% separated lot. In the cup we find pomegranate, hibiscus, and Key lime.

items.title: 2024 Tamiru Tadesse Tesema; SEY x Alo Lot #1, Dry-Fermented Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is one of three very limited lots produced in collaboration with Tamiru and Alo. Only 120 kg of each coffee was produced, making it one of the smallest and most intentional projects we have undertaken in Ethiopia. This coffee is exceptionally complex, with notes of florals, tropical fruits, and tamarind.

items.title: 2024 Tamiru Tadesse Tesema; SEY x Alo Lot #2, Controlled Natural - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is one of three very limited lots produced in collaboration with Tamiru and Alo. Only 120 kg of each coffee was produced, making it one of the smallest and most intentional projects we have undertaken in Ethiopia. This coffee has a fruit-forward profile of orange candy, champagne, and poached pear.

items.title: 2024 Tamiru Tadesse Tesema; SEY x Alo Lot #3, Blanched Natural - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is one of three very limited lots produced in collaboration with Tamiru and Alo. Only 120 kg of each coffee was produced, making it one of the smallest and most intentional projects we have undertaken in Ethiopia. This coffee has the most process-forward profile of the three, with notes of cherry cordial, mulberry, and starfruit.

items.title: 2024 Deison Rodriguez; Filadelfia - Colombia
items.desc: This is a lovely Pink Bourbon selection from our project in San Agustín. This is our first year purchasing from Deison Rodriguez, and it is an honor to bring this lot to market. In the cup we find marmalade, baking spice, and eucalyptus.

items.title: 2024 Wilson Alba; Sierra Morena, 2nd Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This lot comes from the second harvest pass at Sierra Morena this season. It is bright, crisp, and sweet, with pointed lemonade-like acidity, excellent berry complexity, and floral transparency.

items.title: 2024 Kibingo - Burundi NEW
items.desc: This is our second year purchasing coffee from the Kibingo washing station, located in Kayanza—one of the world’s best coffee-growing regions. In the cup we find black tea, Key lime, and clove.

items.title: 2024 Pablo Malacatos; Nueva Esperanza - Ecuador
items.desc: This is an exciting selection from a young producer in southern Ecuador. At just 23 years old, Pablo cultivates coffee on a small 2-hectare (~5-acre) garden. In the cup we find lemon curd, rose water, and pineapple.

items.title: 2024 Alejandro Renjifo; Reina De Saba, Gesha, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This remains one of our favorite Gesha profiles year after year. The seeds were originally hand-selected from a specific Gesha tree in Acevedo, Huila, and planted at high elevations in San Agustín. In the cup we find intoxicating florals, ripe berries, lychee, peach, articulated acidity, and delightful sweetness.

items.title: 2024 Nayith Morales; Beraca - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing coffee from Nayith Morales, who has a very small Pink Bourbon garden, less than a hectare (~2.5 acres), in one of our favorite regions in Huila. In the cup we find strawberry preserves, lemonade, and sugar cane.

items.title: 2024 Chelbessa - Ethiopia
items.desc: As we bid farewell to the Ethiopian coffee season, this is our final selection from one of our favorite sites in Gedeb: Chelbessa. In the cup we find stone fruit, watermelon, and citrus.

items.title: 2024 Enrique Merino; Lugmapata, Mejorado - Ecuador
items.desc: Our work with Lugmapata’s Mejorado has been about discovery. We have come to truly love this coffee, making it the focus of fun and educational processing experiments. Each harvest brings new depth and clarity to these efforts, and we are excited to keep building on this foundation. In this cup we find pineapple, honeysuckle, and strawberry jam.

items.title: 2024 Enrique Merino; Lugmapata, Sidra, New Season - Ecuador
items.desc: We have been working with Sidra from Lugmapata since day one. It is a coffee we have come to love and one that has become central to our ongoing processing experiments, which bring a fun and educational dimension to our work. This experimentation is a work in progress, and will only continue to improve with each harvest! In this year's cup we find lychee, mango, and orange.

items.title: 2024 Kanzu; Lot #21 - Rwanda
items.desc: This coffee comes from Rwanda’s most renowned coffee-producing region, high along the shores of Lake Kivu. Coffees from this area are truly unique. In the cup we find purple fruit, baking spices, black tea, and citrus.

items.title: 2024 Gahahe - Burundi
items.desc: Each year, we eagerly anticipate coffees from Burundi, specifically from Kayanza. Gahahe is an outstanding washing station just south of Kayanza and produces exceptional, terroir-focused profiles. In the cup we find dark fruit, blood orange, and baking spice.

items.title: 2024 Darlin Ariel Guzman - Honduras
items.desc: This selection continues our exploration of the Pacas variety and the Santa Bárbara region. This is our first year purchasing coffee from Darlin Guzman, and we feel this 100% Pacas lot truly represents the potential of this variety and place. In the cup we find plum, raspberry, and lemongrass.

items.title: 2024 La Muralla, Pink Bourbon - Colombia
items.desc: Many producers in La Muralla, a small neighborhood in San Agustín, have planted Pink Bourbon over the years. Many of these lots are small yet showcase excellent quality. This blend of neighboring lots offers a classic Pink Bourbon profile of raspberry, blueberry, and limeade.

items.title: 2024 Keramo, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first release of a honey-processed lot from this special washing station, and a continuation of our exploration of this process with Daye Bensa. The results have been outstanding. In the cup we find watermelon, star fruit, and peach.

items.title: 2024 Marvin Alvarado; La Vistada - Honduras
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing coffee from Marvin Alvarado. This 100% Pacas lot deepens our exploration of this unique variety and mountain region. In the cup we find dark berries, green grape, and nectarine.

items.title: 2024 Diego & Fernando Ucros; El Recreo - Colombia
items.desc: This is a fun Gesha from a unique and underrepresented region in Colombia. Gesha is now planted in many areas, and we expect to see even more from a vast array of places in the future. In the cup we find a floral-driven profile of white flowers, bergamot, and clementine.

items.title: 2024 Laura Rivera; Rivera, Typica - Colombia
items.desc: This is the fourth time we have purchased coffee from the remarkable Laura Rivera. Finding 100% Typica in Colombia is rare, especially when it is organically grown. In the cup we find excellent sweetness, stone fruit, and fresh strawberry.

items.title: 2024 Abelardo Medina; El Girasol, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: Abelardo produced one of our favorite Pink Bourbons last year, and we are extremely excited to be roasting his coffee again. In the cup we find lemonade, ripe blueberry, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2024 Masha - Burundi
items.desc: We are excited to release this season’s first lot from Burundi! This selection comes from the Masha site in Kayanza, near Lake Kivu, a region known for some of the most terroir-specific profiles we encounter in coffee. In the cup we find red tea, baking spice, dried fruit, and citrus.

items.title: 2024 Franci Elena Astaiza; El Casino - Colombia
items.desc: This is the first harvest of the season from Franci Elena. We have worked with coffees from El Casino for many years, but this is the first year we are differentiating releases by harvest pass. In the cup we find strawberry jam, lychee, and honeysuckle.

items.title: 2024 Familia Vallecillo; Los Primos, Catuai - Honduras
items.desc: This 100% Catuai separation is a beautiful example of traditional varieties from Santa Bárbara. In the cup we find plum, raspberry, and candied lemon.

items.title: 2024 Yaye Chericho - Ethiopia
items.desc: Yaye is among the highest-elevation washing stations in the world, and this is our second year sourcing from this small, exceptional site. In the cup we find ripe tropical fruit, lively acidities, and complex botanicals.

items.title: 2024 Norman Castellanos; El Pinabete - Honduras
items.desc: Norman is a second-generation coffee producer we were introduced to during our trip to Honduras this fall. This well-balanced expression of Pacas is bright, with articulated acidity and notes of apricot and plum.

items.title: 2024 Kubi, Anaerobic Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: Our exporting partner Snap created this small experimental anaerobic honey-processed lot for us using carefully selected cherries from the Kubi site in Gedeb. In the cup we find lemon candy, nectarine, and fresh herbs.

items.title: 2024 Salvador Vargas; Chillurco - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year buying coffee from Salvador. It is always exciting to discover new and young producers, especially when they are growing Pink Bourbon at over 1,800 masl! In the cup we find pomegranate, raspberry, and lemon.

items.title: 2024 Estela Pitti; Los Cenizos - Panama
items.desc: This is our first year buying coffee from Estela, and our first Gesha from the Cerra Punta region. Los Cenizos is located beyond Volcán, and produces some of the highest-elevation Gesha in Panama. In the cup we find a lovely profile of watermelon, coffee blossom, nectarine, and lemon.

items.title: 2024 Yoniar Aguilar - Honduras
items.desc: This is our first year buying coffee from Yoniar Aguilar, who grows one of the highest Pacas lots in all of Santa Bárbara. In the cup we find pomegranate, yellow tropical fruit, and excellent sweetness.

items.title: 2024 Juan Medina; El Zancudero, Gesha - Honduras
notes: A floral profile of white tea
items.desc: This beautiful representation of Gesha from Santa Bárbara is the first coffee we have purchased from Juan Medina. In the cup we find a floral profile of white tea, watermelon, and citrus.

items.title: 2024 Ernedis Rodriguez; El Paraiso, Sidra - Colombia
items.desc: This is our second season working with this 100% Sidra separation from El Paraiso, and the profile is really starting to develop and mature. In the cup we find raspberries, eucalyptus, and peach.

items.title: 2024 Peterson & Purity Muthathai; Ngaratua Estate, AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: Ngaratua consistently produces complex and dynamic profiles and has quickly become one of our favorite single estates to work with in Kenya. This lot is essentially pure SL28 and sings of dark fruits, citrus, and subtle florality.

items.title: 2024 Finca Sophia; Lot #47 - Panama
items.desc: We are highly impressed with the intentionality behind this natural-processed lot from Finca Sophia. In the cup we find an exceptionally clean, fruit-forward profile of strawberry, blueberry, jasmine, and peach.

items.title: 2024 Finca Sophia; Lot #48 & Lot #18 - Panama
items.desc: We purchased our three favorite washed lots from Finca Sophia this year. Two were so small (8 kg and 2 kg, respectively) that we had to blend them together to roast. The result is an elegant, traditional Gesha profile with a very aromatic cup of white florals, tropical fruit, and berries, all with excellent structure.

items.title: 2024 Finca Sophia; Lot #41 - Panama
items.desc: This 15 kg lot is one of three washed lots we purchased from Finca Sophia this season. It is vibrant and effervescent, with excellent structure and acidity. In the cup we find a complex profile of florals, mango, and star fruit.

items.title: 2024 La Muralla, Gesha - Colombia
items.desc: Many producers in La Muralla, a small neighborhood in San Agustín, have planted small amounts of Gesha over the years. These lots are typically small but of excellent quality. This blend of neighboring lots offers a traditional Gesha profile of jasmine, ripe peach, and lemon zest.

items.title: 2024 Jose Martinez; El Casino, New Season (1st Harvest) - Colombia
items.desc: We are excited to finally explore something we have always aimed for: separating lots not just by quality, but also by harvest pass. In this exceptional Pink Bourbon, we find strawberry jam, yellow tropical acidity, and a lovely, complex finish.

items.title: 2024 Wilson Alba; Sierra Morena, New Season (1st Harvest) - Colombia
items.desc: This lot is from the first harvest pass at Sierra Morena this season. It is bright, crisp, and sweet, with pointed lemonade-like acidity, excellent berry complexity, and floral transparency.

items.title: 2024 Hamasho, SEY Dry Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: Our goal with this lot was to achieve as complex and dynamic a profile as possible in a washed coffee. This involved an array of experiments with cherry selection, dry fermentation, and drying techniques. In the cup we find melon, peach, and white florals.

items.title: 2024 Hamasho, SEY Dry Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: Our goal with this lot was to explore the possibilities of the honey process while maintaining a clean profile. We selected brighter cherries (with lower Brix) and minimized unwanted fermentation both in-cherry and during the initial drying stage. In the cup we find watermelon, peach rings, and yellow florals.

items.title: 2024 Mbature Family; Kamavindi - Kenya
items.desc: We have tasted the Gesha from this farm since it was first planted. The trees are still quite young, but this is the first year they produced enough for us to roast. There is only 11 kg of this coffee—so little that we brought it back from Kamavindi in our suitcase last winter. In the cup we find yellow florals, chamomile, red currant, honeydew, and watermelon.

items.title: 2024 José Gallardo; Nuguo, Plano Plot - Panama
items.desc: José Gallardo is one of the most revered producers in Panama. His coffees are featured throughout the competition world and achieve some of the highest scores year after year in the Best of Panama. This is an extremely small 16kg lot from a single harvest pass. In the cup we find an intensely floral profile of jasmine and rose, Meyer lemon, and bergamot, with a slightly tropical finish.

items.title: 2024 Hamasho, SEY Traditional Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This traditional honey-processed lot comes from Hamasho, one of our favorite sites in Bensa. Selected and processed specifically for SEY, it is the first of three special preparation lots we collaborated on with Hamasho this year. In the cup we find sweet melon, tropical fruits, and complex florality.

items.title: 2024 Bensa Segera - Ethiopia
items.desc: Coffees from Bensa have risen to the top of the coffee industry in recent years, with nearly all the coffees dominating the Ethiopian Cup of Excellence coming from this region. In the cup we find ripe stone fruit, lemon zest, florality, and berries.

items.title: The Jijon-Quan coffee!
items.desc:
This fully washed Sidra was selected and processed in collaboration with Pepe, Jose, and Brian! They graciously asked us to roast this lot for them—and we gladly accepted. In the cup we find white tea, lime zest, and mint.
From Brian: " Thank you so much for picking up this coffee and watching the videos of my trip to Ecuador to visit Finca Soledad. This was my first time at origin, and I learned so much. This washed Sidra is a testament to the effort and love that everyone at Finca Soledad puts into their coffee. Special thanks to Robert Asami for accompanying me to Ecuador. Thank you to Pepe

items.title: 2024 Hacienda La Esmeralda; Mario Arriba - Panama
items.desc: We are proud to offer this special micro lot from Hacienda La Esmeralda’s Mario Arriba. This Gesha selection showcases a classic Gesha profile: intensely aromatic, with notes of jasmine, lavender, and orange blossom mingling with flavors of peach and bergamot.

items.title: 2024 Ticuna; El Esquilino, Field Blend - Colombia
items.desc: It is rare and fun to taste all of these profiles together. This year’s production was small, so we created this super blend from tiny, highest-quality lots. The result is a deep, almost jam-like sweetness with blueberry, pink grapefruit, and herbal notes.

items.title: 2024 Ibonia Estate; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing coffee from the renowned Ibonia Estate in Kiambu. This fun new selection tastes of hibiscus, red berries, and rosehips.

items.title: 2024 Bombe - Ethiopia
items.desc: Coffees from Bombe are grown at extreme elevations nestled in the valleys of the Sidama mountains. This unique location consistently produces some of the highest-scoring coffees of the year. In the cup we find watermelon, white florals, and raspberry.

items.title: 2024 Kubi, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: Kubi consistently produces some of our favorite coffee each season. This honey-processed selection is remarkably clean. In the cup we find integrated tropical fruit, jasmine pearls, and stone fruit.

items.title: 2024 Daniel Caro Lopez; El Tambo - Colombia
items.desc: This is another very good expression of Chiroso from the Caro family in Anzá. In the cup we find a yellow tropical profile with notes of tamarind and rose.

items.title: 2024 Jhon Alexander Bermudez; Finca La Estrella, Late Late - Colombia
items.desc: Jhon Alexander Bermudez's Chiroso continues to have one of the most unique profiles we have found in Colombia. It is reminiscent of coffees typically found in southern Ethiopia, packed with ripe pineapple, bright acidity, and hops.

items.title: 2024 Buncho - Ethiopia
items.desc: This selection comes from a site owned and operated by Asefa Dukamo, who has produced some of the best honey-processed coffees we have tasted in Ethiopia. In the cup we find watermelon, red tea, and orange zest.

items.title: 2024 Abelardo Medina; El Girasol - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year buying coffee from Abelardo. We discovered his coffee through our buying project in southern Huila, and look forward to working more closely together next season. In the cup we find a sparkling Pink Bourbon profile of lemonade, blueberry, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2024 David Berrio; La Casita, Late Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: David Berrio’s farm, La Casita, is the most remote site we work with in Urrao. The 1.5-hectare (~3.7 acres) farm, more accurately described as a garden, sits at extreme elevation. In the cup we find lively acidity, ripe peach, and berry-like complexity.

items.title: 2024 Keramo - Ethiopia
items.desc: This selection comes from the increasingly renowned Bombe Mountains in Sidama, Bensa, Ethiopia. In the cup we find ripe peach, lemongrass, and blueberry.

items.title: 2024 Nadeia Guerra x Lost Origin; Jaramillo - Panama
items.desc: This is the second release of the ‘makers’ project, a collaboration between Lost Origin and producer Nadeia Guerra. This lot was meticulously processed in a laboratory from only the very best cherry selections. In the cup we find an intoxicating floral profile of jasmine, lavender, and star fruit.

items.title: 2024 Marua; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is one of the highest-scoring coffees we tasted from Kenya this year, and it is the first we have purchased from the Marua site in Nyeri. In the cup we find a more traditional Kenyan profile of black currant, blood orange, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2024 Luis Arnulfo Caro; Hoyo Rico - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year purchasing coffee from Luis Caro, brother of Jose Arcadio Caro. This is also our first selection from the mountains slightly east of Urrao in Anzá. In the cup we find the tropical profile we associate with Chiroso: mango, lychee, and red tea.

items.title: 2024 Jose Arcadio Caro; El Cedral, Late Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This short-stature Chiroso separation is a clean and crisp representation of this variety. In the cup we find an orange citrus and pomegranate profile with an effervescent clarity.

items.title: 2024 Worka - Ethiopia
items.desc: This selection comes from one of our favorite Ethiopian washing stations, high up in the mountains of Gedeb—just south of the famous Yirgacheffe region. Gedeb had an exceptionally strong year. In the cup we find ripe stone fruit, oxidized oolong tea and watermelon.

items.title: 2024 Rumudamo - Ethiopia
items.desc: Rumudamo is located high in Arbegona, a region we have focused on intensely for the last few years. The site gained global fame two years ago by winning Ethiopia’s inaugural Cup of Excellence competition. In this cup we find lavender, nectarine, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2024 Roque Acosta; El Mirador - Colombia
items.desc: This clean and structured Pink Bourbon from Roque Acosta is a new discovery from our exploration of San Agustín, Huila. In the cup we find an articulated profile of citrus, raspberry, and oolong tea.

items.title: 2024 Bekele Belaychow; Hora Ganet - Ethiopia
items.desc: This special micro lot is one of the very few fully traceable single-producer, single-variety lots we have ever purchased from Ethiopia. It is also the first lot Bekele produced using a de-pulper. In the cup we find tropical fruits like mango and mandarin with red tea florality.

items.title: 2024 Diego Hoyos; La Fortuna, Late Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: We are honored to continue working with Diego’s coffees, which have been in high demand since winning several regional competitions in southern Huila. This late harvest separation offers bright fruits, lively acidity, and jam-like sweetness.

items.title: 2024 Alejandro Renjifo; Reina De Saba, Gesha - Colombia
items.desc: This remains one of our favorite Gesha profiles year after year. The seeds were initially hand-selected from a specific Gesha tree in Acevedo and planted high up in San Agustín. This harvest, we taste a more fruit-forward strawberry profile with florality and bright yellow acidity.

items.title: 2024 Kubi - Ethiopia
items.desc: We have been working with Kubi for years, and this selection comes from a small regional group of producers who deliver to the Chelbessa washing station, which regularly produces some of our favorite Ethiopian coffees. In the cup we find intoxicating florals, watermelon, peach, and lively citrus acidity.

items.title: 2024 Servio Botina; El Cedro - Late Late Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is the first year we have worked with Servio Botina after discovering his coffee at a regional competition in Huila. His coffees continue to exceed expectations, and we are excited to work with this lot from his late harvest. In the cup we find blackberry, wildflower honey, and excellent density.

items.title: 2024 Gathaithi; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is our second year purchasing coffee from the Gathaithi site in Nyeri. Most of the coffees we have tasted from Kenya this year—including this one—have had a much softer profile than those of years past. In the cup we find a yellow profile of tropical fruit, tea, and honey.

items.title: 2024 Arles Jair Galindez; El Guayabo - Colombia
items.desc: Our first coffee from the Galindez family immediately impressed us with its level of expression and complexity. In the cup we find a Kenya-like profile of blackcurrant, rose hips, and pomegranate.

items.title: 2024 Banko Chelchele - Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot is exclusively from the community of Banko, a small kebele (neighborhood) delivering to the Chelbessa washing station in Gedeb—a region known for producing some of our favorite coffees. In the cup we find ripe stone fruit, florals, and melon.

items.title: 2024 Jose & Pepe Jijon; Finca San Pedro, Middle Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the middle harvest from father and son Pepe and Jose Jijon's new farm, Finca San Pedro. Jose is an inspired young coffee producer, and we are incredibly excited to see what the future holds for him. San Pedro is one of the most beautiful farms we have ever seen, at some of the highest elevations we have ever seen coffee produced in Ecuador. In the cup we find very clean tropical fruit, rose, and raspberry.

items.title: 2024 Francisco Vintimilla & Pepe Jijon; Finca Surya, Middle Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: Finca Surya sits directly next to Pepe Jijon's new farm, San Pedro. We have worked with several harvests from Francisco in the past and are excited to see these two passionate producers come together to create extraordinary lots. This middle-season lot is comprised of cherry harvested from April 1st through 5th. In the cup we find white florals, pear, and melon.

items.title: 2024 Jose Martinez; El Casino, Late Late Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: We are excited to finally be exploring something we have always wanted to explore: separating lots not just by quality, but also by harvest pass. This coffee is from the last harvest pass at El Casino. In this exceptional Pink Bourbon we find ripe red fruit, yellow tropical acidity, and a lovely complex finish.

items.title: 2024 Danche, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our first attempt at making a honey process at Danche, and the experiment really paid off! This lot is clean, articulate, and very expressive. In the cup we find ripe berries, lively acidity, and nectarine.

items.title: 2024 Halo Hartume - Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot stays on the bright, crisp, and cleaner side of the profiles we see from Gedeb: a plethora of light fruit tones complemented by soft floral tea notes. The fruit notes hover between light peach and tropical, with hints of tart plum and other stone fruits.

items.title: 2024 Ricardo Silva; Finca El Suspiro, Pink Bourbon - Colombia
items.desc: Ricardo is the first producer we've worked with in the region of Algeciras, Huila, and his Gesha lot that we released earlier this year was a stunner! In the cup we find Rainier cherry, Key lime, and blueberry.

items.title: 2024 Danche - Ethiopia
items.desc: Danche is just a few kilometers from the famed Chelbessa washing station, and similarly produces immaculate coffees year after year. In the cup we find intoxicating florals, watermelon, peach, and a lively citrus acidity.

items.title: 2024 Valentim & Edneia Fiorese - Brazil
items.desc: This first-place competition-winning lot from Bateia, Espiríto Santo, is our final Brazilian release of the season. In the cup we find blackberry, tropical fruit, and a delightful acidity.

items.title: 2024 Chelchele - Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot is exclusively comprised of deliveries from Chelchele — a small kebele (neighborhood) that delivers to the Chelbessa washing station, which is located in a region that produces some of our favorite coffees each year: Gadeb. In the cup we find ripe stone fruit, green florals, and melon.

items.title: 2024 Gildardo Lopez; El Calamar - Late Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: Gildardo has won many regional competitions, including the inaugural Copa de Oro. He is a very sought-after producer, and this expressive Pink Bourbon cup exemplifies why: excellently articulated acidities, a complex finish, and strawberry preserves throughout.

items.title: 2024 Worka Chelbessa; Lot #10 - Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot comes from one of our favorite washing stations high up in the mountains of Gedeb—just south of the famous Yirgacheffe region. In the cup we find ripe stone fruit, nectarine, peach, oolong tea, and watermelon.

items.title: 2024 Banko Gotiti - Ethiopia
items.desc: We have been working in Banko Gotiti for several years, and love the cleanliness, brightness, and elegance of the coffees the region produces. In this cup we find wildflower honey, tangerine, and apricot.

items.title: 2024 Marcos Nali & Luciana Aparecida - Brazil
items.desc: As we continue exploring Espiríto Santo, we find ourselves returning to the area of Bateia and the standout coffees it produces. This single-bag auction lot is an excellent example of why. In the cup we find pomegranate, blueberry, and lemon zest.

items.title: 2024 Fabiano Nali; Sítio Nali - Brazil
items.desc: We are very excited to welcome Brazil back to our menu, beginning with this lot from one of our favorite micro-regions in Espírito Santo: Bateia. In the cup we find red currant, orange blossom, and red tea.

items.title: 2024 Edivaldo Cunha; Sítio Alto Ribeirão - Brazil
items.desc: We have been working with Edivaldo for a few years now, and he consistently produces some of the highest-quality coffee we see in Espírito Santo. In this cup we find hibiscus, sweet cranberry, and honey.

items.title: 2024 Bukeye - Burundi
items.desc: This separation from Long Miles Coffee Project is a blend of the best cherries delivered to the Bukeye washing station from all of the surrounding hills. Bukeye produces some of our favorite coffee in Burundi, and this classic profile is exemplary of why. In the cup we find red tea, blood orange, and clove.

items.title: 2024 Disnely Maria Gutierez; La Bonanza - Colombia
items.desc: This is another delightful Chiroso lot from our ongoing project in Urrao. Disnely's garden of 1,800 coffee trees is directly next to her house, and she does all of the processing herself. In the cup we find tropical fruit, lemon verbena, and ripe strawberry.

items.title: Jose & Pepe Jijon; Finca San Pedro - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the very first release from father and son Pepe and Jose Jijon's new farm, Finca San Pedro. It is humbling and a true honor to have the first opportunity to work with this coffee. Jose is an inspired young coffee producer, and we are extremely excited to see what the future holds for him. San Pedro is one of the most beautiful farms we have ever seen, at some of the highest elevations we have ever seen coffee produced in Ecuador. In the cup we find white florals, pear, and yellow fruit.

items.title: 2024 Francisco Vintimilla & Pepe Jijon; Finca Surya - Ecuador
items.desc: This farm sits directly next to Pepe Jijon's new farm, San Pedro. We have worked with several harvests from Francisco in the past, and are extremely excited to see these two passionate producers come together to create this special lot. In the cup we find lightly fermented mango, pineapple, citrus, and tea-like florals.

items.title: 2024 John Carvajal; El Guadualito - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first release of the variety Aji — a newer variety being cultivated in Huila. Aji has been genetically identified as 100% Ethiopian Landrace, and we are extremely excited to see the diversity of varieties in Colombia continue to grow! In the cup we find vibrant acidity, ripe stone fruit, and green grape.

items.title: 2024 Ngugu-ini; AB Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first Kenyan of the season, and our first ever lot from the washing station of Ngugu-ini in the community of Kirinyaga. In the cup we find darker fruit typical of Kenyan coffee, lemon-like acidity, and excellent depth and complexity.

items.title: 2024 Servio Botina; El Cedro - Colombia
items.desc: This lot is how we were introduced to Servio Botina! This is his Copa de Oro competition lot, which was one of our highest-scoring coffees in the competition. In the cup we find dark berries, bright acidity, and a long and complex profile.

items.title: 2024 Monica Figueroa; El Guamal - Colombia
items.desc: Our first coffee from Monica Figueroa is a really lovely Chiroso with great depth of sweetness and a slightly softer acidity. In the cup we find lemongrass, black tea, and mango.

items.title: 2024 Jorge Eliécer Alba Imbachi; Sierra Morena - Colombia
items.desc: This harvesting and cherry selection represented in this Pink Bourbon lot is as close to perfect as we have seen in Colombia. The cup is bright, crisp, and sweet, with a pointed lemonade-like acidity, excellent berry complexity and a floral transparency.

items.title: 2024 Ernedis Rodriguez; El Paraiso - Colombia
items.desc: Although we have been working with Ernedis and his farm, El Paraiso, for several years, this is the first time we have purchased his Sidra to share with you. In the cup we find raspberry preserves, lemon, and white florals.

items.title: 2024 Jose Arcadio Caro; El Cedral - Colombia
items.desc: This short-stature Chiroso separation is a very clean and crisp representation of this variety. In the cup we find a very orange citrus and mango profile with an effervescent clarity.

items.title: 2024 Heza; Nkonge Hill, Reserve Lot #2 - Burundi
items.desc: Of the many lots the Long Miles team tasted this year, only five were separated out as "Reserve". This is one of those lots, and it is the highest-scoring lot we tasted from Burundi this season. In the cup we find Kenya-like blackcurrant and complex layered acidities.

items.title: 2024 Juan Jiménez; El Porvenir, Late - Colombia
items.desc: Juan Jiménez's coffees continue to impress beyond words, and this season has been extraordinary for him and his farm. In the cup we find limeade, lilac, and lychee.

items.title: 2024 Jhon Alexander Bermudez; Finca La Estrella, Late - Colombia
items.desc: Jhon Alexander Bermudez's Chiroso continues to have one of the most unique profiles we've found in Colombia. It is far more reminiscent of coffees we typically find in southern Ethiopia, packed with ripe blueberry, very bright acidity, and hops.

items.title: La Familia Morales Rivera; Cruz Loma - Ecuador
items.desc: We made this fun blend by combining a washed anaerobic Sidra and Mejorado lot with a natural-processed Sidra lot. The result is a clean dynamic profile with an added fruit complexity. In the cup we find peach, lemonade, and Concord grape.

items.title: 2024 Penderisco - Colombia
items.desc: We created this lot by combining very small deliveries from multiple producers. As our work continues in Urrao, we have been lucky to meet many new producers. However, some harvests are too small to fully separate and export. This cup presents vibrant yellow tropical fruit with excellent sweetness and acidity.

items.title: 2024 Ricardo Silva; Finca El Suspiro - Colombia
items.desc: This extraordinary Gesha selection is the first coffee we've ever tasted from Ricardo, and it is a stunner. It is intensely sweet and aromatic, with white jasmine florals, confectioners' sugar, and tangerine.

items.title: 2024 Ninga; Bumba Hill, Lot #8 - Burundi
items.desc: This is our first year working with coffee from the extremely remote Bumba Hill, and it is the only selection we made from the Ninga washing station this year. In the cup, we find dried apricots, baking spice, and Earl Gray.

items.title: 2024 Franci Elena; El Casino - Colombia
items.desc: This Pink Bourbon selection is another release from our incentive purchasing project in Huila, which began during our trip there last fall. In the cup we find sweet citrus, lychee, and raspberry.

items.title: 2024 Fabian Rodriguez; Filadelfia - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first time purchasing coffee from Fabian. This coffee was one of our top-scoring lots in this year's Copa de Oro competition, and we are honored to showcase it for you. In the cup we find a malic acidity, ripe strawberry, and rose.

items.title: 2024 Soranyi Lorena; El Tesoro - Colombia
items.desc: We are honored to have a very small allocation of this Copa de Oro lot from Soranyi. This coffee was amongst our highest-scoring lots presented in the competition. In the cup we find an interesting herbal profile with yellow tropical fruit, ripe melon, and eucalyptus.

items.title: 2024 Heza; Gitwe Hill, Lot #1 - Burundi
items.desc: The coffees from Gitwe Hill are traditionally some of our favorites, and this fermented honey selection is no exception! In the cup we find purple fruit, black tea, and baking spice.

items.title: 2024 Rolando Moroccolla - Peru
items.desc: This is our second Gesha lot from Peru this season. While having a different profile, it is equally impressive and really shows this region's diversity. In the cup we find a very floral Gesha profile of jasmine and honeysuckle, sparking clean acidities, and excellent structure.

items.title: 2024 Ilmer Gomez; El Tesoro - Colombia
items.desc: We have been working in La Muralla since our inception, but this is our first time working with Ilmer. It remains an amazing experience to meet new producers and work with new coffees from a region we have come to know so well. In the cup we find purple fruit, orange zest, and grape.

items.title: 2024 Las Orquideas - Colombia
items.desc: This is a unique blend we created from very small deliveries from multiple different producers. As our work continues in Urrao, we have been lucky to meet many new producers. However, some harvests are too small to fully separate and export. This cup's profile is floral, clean, and elegant.

items.title: 2024 Yoan Arley Toledo; Los Andes - Colombia
items.desc: We are excited to showcase this Copa de Oro competition lot from Yoan––a young producer from one of our favorite regions in Huila: Suaza. In the cup we find ripe papaya, layered florality, and stone fruit.

items.title: 2024 Juan Jiménez; El Porvenir - Colombia
items.desc: We are honored to have a very small allocation of this exquisite high-scoring Pink Bourbon lot from the Copa de Oro competition. In the cup we find excellent structure and sweetness, lemon acidity, tea-like florality, and mango.

items.title: 2024 Enrique Merino; Lugmapata, L1 - Ecuador
items.desc: This is an interesting new variety from Lugmapata. This variety was discovered growing in a random coffee plot, isolated, and slowly, over the last six years, has been planted into a lot of its own. The cup profile and potential are very good, and developing this is one of the most exciting long-term projects we have been part of. In the cup we find yellow tropical fruit and bright citrus acidity.

items.title: 2024 Enrique Merino; Lugmapata, Sidra - Ecuador
items.desc: We have been working with Sidra from Lugmapata from day one. It is a coffee that we have come to love, and also one we have begun to run extremely fun and educational processing experiments with. This experimentation is a work in progress and will only continue to improve with each harvest! In the cup we find lychee, mango, and orange.

items.title: 2024 Heza; Mutana Hill, Lot #1 - Burundi
items.desc: Mutana's hills border the Kibira Forest, and are truly breathtaking to behold. This lot is made up of five distinct harvest deliveries, referred to as “day lots”. In the cup we find a really long profile of baked fruit, mulling spices, and tea.

items.title: 2024 Heza; Mikuba Hill - Burundi
items.desc: This exceptionally clean fermented honey selection from the Mikuba site has a slightly brighter profile. In the cup we find red berries, orange blossom, and mulled citrus.

items.title: 2024 Mario Asorza - Peru
items.desc: This is one of the most impressive coffees we've tasted from Peru. We have been exploring Peru for a few years now with varying degrees of success, but something magical is happening here. The cup is a more fruit-forward gesha profile; still very floral, but with added berry complexity and sweetness.

items.title: 2024 Mayor Domo; La Granada - Colombia
items.desc: This extraordinary Pink Bourbon lot is as close to perfect harvesting and cherry selection as we have seen in Colombia. It is bright, crisp, and sweet, with a pointed lemonade-like acidity, excellent berry complexity and a floral transparency.

items.title: 2024 Bukeye; Munyinya Hill, Lot #2 - Burundi
items.desc: Munyinya Hill was the coffee that first drew our attention to this region many years ago. It remains one of our favorite sites to buy coffee from, and we look forward to the arrival of this coffee every year. In the cup we find clementine, oxodized oolong, and currants.

items.title: 2024 Heza; Nkonge Hill, Lot #1 - Burundi
items.desc: It isn't easy to express how much we love coffees from the Heza washing station, and this lot from Nkonge Hill is consistently one of our favorites. In the cup we find a traditional red tea profile, along with blood orange, blackberry, and mulling spices.

items.title: 2024 Octavio Rueda; El Mirador - Colombia
items.desc: Octavio's coffee stood out during our last buying trip to Colombia. There are several distinct Pink Bourbon profiles at this point, and this is one of our favorites. In the cup we find pink lemonade, berries, and black tea.

items.title: 2024 Jorge Cortes; Chiquito - Colombia
items.desc: Tabi is still a relatively new variety that is almost exclusively cultivated in Colombia. This is our first time working with this variety from the terroir of Nariño. In the cup we find cherry, cacao, and pink grapefruit.

items.title: 2024 Yesica Moreno; Finca El Rosal - Colombia
items.desc: We have been focusing on Urrao for several years and have come to believe that some of the most complex coffees in the world come from this region. In this cup we find the classic tropical Chiroso profile of peach tea and subtle florality.

items.title: 2024 David Berrio; La Casita - Colombia
items.desc: David Berrio's 1.5-hectare (~3.7 acres) garden is by far the most remote site we work with in Urrao. This separation is from his late harvest, and sings of ripe tropical fruits with a lively acidity and berry-like complexity.

items.title: 2024 Jhon Alexander Bermudez; Finca La Estrella - Colombia
items.desc: This coffee from Jhon Alexander Bermudez continues to have one of the most unique profiles we've found in Colombia; far more reminiscent of a profile we typically only find in southern Ethiopia. In the cup we find ripe peach, very bright acidity, and hops.

items.title: 2023 José Martinez; El Casino, Pink Bourbon, Late - Colombia
items.desc: José Martinez consistently produces some of our favorite Pink Bourbon, and this season's harvest is no different. The cup is fruit-forward, with sparkling acidity and notes of pink grapefruit, mango, and berries.

items.title: 2024 Guillermo Lomas - Ecuador
items.desc: This is our third year working with Guillermo, and the quality of his coffee continues to be outstanding. This 100% Sidra selection is an excellent representation of this unique variety. In the cup we find eucalyptus, red berries, and citrus.

items.title: 2024 Marino Ruiz; Buena Vista - Colombia
items.desc: We met Marino Ruiz on our visit to Huila last fall. He and his family have a beautiful farm that rests on the cliffs of Pital. This is one of many new Pink Bourbons we are releasing this season as we really start to dive deep on this region and variety. In the cup we find dried strawberry, lemon, and raspberry.

items.title: 2023 Juan Peña; La Papaya, Mejorado - Ecuador
items.desc: We have been working with Juan Peña's La Papaya since we began, and it has always held a very special place in our hearts. In this season's cup we find black tea, candied lemon, and raspberry.

items.title: 2024 Kibingo - Burundi
items.desc: This is our first Burundian selection of the season! This lot comes from the Kibingo washing station in a place we consider to be one of the best places to grow coffee in the world: Kayanza. In the cup we find black tea, Key lime, and clove.

items.title: 2023 Erick Bravo; Finca El Chaferote, Late - Colombia
items.desc: This is our third season working with the coffees from Erick Bravo, and his Pink Bourbon continues to be one of our favorite expressions of the variety. In the cup we find a classic Pink Bourbon profile of bright citrus, ripe stone fruit, and berries.

items.title: 2023 Wilson Alba; Sierra Morena - Colombia
items.desc: This extraordinary representation of Pink Bourbon is as close to perfect harvesting and cherry selection as we have seen in Colombia. It is bright, crisp, and sweet, with a pointed lemonade-like acidity, excellent berry complexity and a floral transparency.

items.title: 2023 The Moreno Family; Piedras Amarillas - Honduras
items.desc: This is the late, higher-elevation harvest from Piedras Amarillas—a farm we have worked with for seven years now. In the cup we taste lychee, black raspberry, and orange blossom honey.

items.title: 2023 Regina Narvaez; El Limon - Colombia
items.desc: Regina is a younger producer who is part of a new project we are working on in one of our favorite regions of Colombia: Nariño. This lot is the first Pink Bourbon we have been able to bring in from the region. In the cup we find a lively citrus acidity, Rainier cherry, and raspberry.

items.title: 2023 Ernedis Rodriguez; El Paraiso - Colombia
items.desc: Caturra is one of our favorite varieties, and it has become increasingly challenging to grow. Over the next few years, we plan to continue investing in producers like Ernedis who also have a special place in their hearts for this variety. In the cup we taste cooked strawberry, pear, and lemon verbena.

items.title: 2023 Rita Lopez; Betania - Colombia
items.desc: Rita Lopez is a young producer with excellent potential, and we are glad she is part of a new project we are working on in Nariño—one of our favorite but most challenging origins in Colombia. In the cup we find a traditional profile for Colombia: plum and honeydew with a delicate malic acidity.

items.title: 2023 Abel Salinas; Arashi - Ecuador
items.desc: This is a beautiful, transparent, and clean representation of Mejorado from one of our favorite regions in Ecuador. In the cup the profile is elegant and refined, with layers of soft florals, peach, and lemon.

items.title: 2023 Diana Sofia Jimenez; La Esperanza - Colombia
items.desc: We work very hard to offer single variety separations. But, in this case, the harvest was too small to separate, and we were intrigued by the very unique blend of some of our favorite varieties. In the cup we find a complete profile of rose, cooked berries, and clementine.

items.title: 2023 Laboyano - Colombia
items.desc: Laboyano is a cool blend of tiny, high-scoring lots that were too small to separate and export independently. Each constituent lot is the highest-quality cherry from each of a group of producers in the valley of Laboyano. In the cup, we find a caramel-like sweetness, tangerine, and raspberry.

items.title: 2023 Pepe Jijon; Finca Soledad, Sidra - Ecuador
items.desc: This 100% Sidra selection from Pepe Jijon's biodynamic farm in northern Ecuador is as inspiring as its story. The profile is delicate, floral, and citrusy.

items.title: 2023 Pepe Jijon; Finca Soledad, Mejorado - Ecuador
items.desc: This is another stunning release from Pepe Jijon. His innovative processing techniques produce remarkably clean and vibrant profiles reminiscent of coffees from Kenya or the best of Espírito Santo. In the cup we find currants, hibiscus, and a vibrant, articulated structure.

items.title: 2023 Diego Hoyos; La Fortuna, Late - Colombia
items.desc: We are honored to continue working with Diego's coffees, which have been in high demand since winning several regional competitions in Southern Huila. In the cup we find bright fruits, lively acidity, and a jam-like sweetness.

items.title: 2023 Halo Hartume - Ethiopia
items.desc: This washed profile stays on the bright, crisp, and cleaner side of the profiles we see from Gedeb; a plethora of light fruit tones complemented by soft floral tea notes. The fruit notes hover between light peach and tropical, and have hints of tart plum and other stone fruits.

items.title: 2023 Chelchele - Ethiopia
items.desc: Gedeb produces some of the best coffees in the world, which is why we've been working there for several years. This is our first year working with the Chelchele washing station, and we're very pleased with this cup of peach candy, jasmine pearls, and cantaloupe.

items.title: 2023 Alejandro Renjifo; Reina De Saba, Caturra - Colombia
items.desc: The harvest from Reina de Saba is one we look forward to every year. It is one of our favorite farms in one of our favorite producing regions. This Caturra separation has excellently structured sweetness and acidity, with notes of papaya and citrus.

items.title: 2023 Pepe Jijon; Finca Soledad, Gesha - Ecuador
items.desc: This is Pepe Jijon's first year of Gesha production, and it is an honor to have the opportunity to work with it! The cup is fruit-forward, with flavors of fermented tropical fruits, delicate florals, and deep sweetness.

items.title: 2023 Juan Peña; La Papaya, Gesha - Ecuador
items.desc: This is the first year Juan Peña has produced a washed Gesha, and we're very excited to work with this expression of this variety grown on this now legendary farm. This cup is remarkably complex, with yellow tropical fruits, classic Gesha florality, and a lovely citrus acidity.

items.title: 2023 Yaye Chericho - Ethiopia
items.desc: Yaye is one of the highest-elevation washing stations in the world. We have been increasing our efforts in this region for several years, and this is one of the coffees that has finally paid off. This coffee screams in the cup: ripe tropical fruit, lively acidities, and botanicals.

items.title: 2023 Kadir Jabril; Wate Gogugu - Ethiopia
items.desc: The coffee trees in Wate Gogogu are only five to ten years old—some of Ethiopia's youngest. These younger trees, the extreme altitudes, and Kadir Jabril’s inimitable focus on quality all together result in an exceptionally complex coffee. In the cup we find intoxicating honeysuckle, passion fruit, and a lively citrus acidity.

items.title: 2023 Kanzu - Rwanda
items.desc: This coffee comes from the most famous coffee-producting region in Rwanda, high up along the shores of Lake Kivu. Coffees from this region are extremely unique. In the cup we find purple fruit, baking spices, black tea, and citrus.

items.title: 2023 Danny Moreno; Los Andes, Gesha - Honduras
items.desc: This is the late, higher-elevation harvest from Piedras Amarillas—a farm we have worked with for seven years now. In the cup we taste lychee, black raspberry, and orange blossom honey.

items.title: 2023 Ticuna; El Mirado - Colombia
items.desc: This is a 100% Pink Bourbon separation from our friends José and Kyle's farm, El Mirador. In the cup we find a deep, jam-like sweetness, ripe berries, pink grapefruit, and subtle orange blossom.

items.title: 2023 Misael Ochoa; Mis Peñitas - Honduras
items.desc: We were introduced to Misael Ochoa during our visit to San Vicente this spring, and were impressed by this 100% Bourbon separation. In the cup we find soft florality, raspberry, and brown sugar.

items.title: 2023 José Martinez; El Casino, Caturra - Colombia
items.desc: José Martinez consistently produces some of our favorite Pink Bourbon, and this harvest is no different. The cup is fruit-forward, with sparkling acidity and notes of pink grapefruit, mango, and berries.

items.title: 2022 Mbature Family; Kamavindi, AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is a single-estate AA selection from the Mbature family on the southeastern slopes of Mt. Kenya. Working with this family's coffee is a dream and an honor, as their production and processing are among the best we've ever seen. In the cup we find a darker profile of blackcurrant, florals, and plum.

items.title: 2023 Sebastián Velazco Rodriguez - Mexico
items.desc: Sebastian grows his coffee within the forest of the Sierra Mazateca. His farm is fully organic, and teeming with biodiversity. In the cup we find a comforting profile of chocolate, blueberry, and a balanced citrus acidity.

items.title: 2023 Hamasho, Extended Fermentation - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a really interesting extended fermentation coffee from one of the most highly regarded washing stations in all of Ethiopia. In the cup we find ripe watermelon, peach candy, and a lovely balanced acidity.

items.title: 2023 José Martinez; El Casino, Pink Bourbon - Colombia
items.desc: José Martinez consistently produces some of our favorite Pink Bourbon, and this harvest is no different. The cup is fruit-forward, with sparkling acidity and notes of pink grapefruit, mango, and berries.

items.title: 2023 Bitalina Lopez; Finca Bitalina, Late - Honduras
items.desc: Bitalina has an extremely small coffee garden of .3 hectares (.75 acres) where she grows both Pacas and the traditional Bourbon. Her coffee is, in a word, remarkable, every single year. In the cup we find pomegranate and plum, with a delightfully subtle florality.

items.title: 2023 Faiber Cordoba; Los Naranjos, Late - Colombia
items.desc: This is our third year working with Faiber’s coffee. He is an exceptionally talented young producer growing an impressive array of varieties. In the cup we find a fruit-forward profile, excellent sweetness and acidity, and notes of strawberry jam, Key lime, and blackberry.

items.title: 2023 Hamasho, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot comes from staggering elevations in the beautiful Bombe Mountains in one of the regions of Ethiopia we have been the most excited about: Bensa, Sidama. In the cup we find a very floral, expressive, and refreshing profile of chamomile and nectarine, with a long limeade finish.

items.title: 2023 Gildardo Lopez; El Calamar, Late - Colombia
items.desc: Gildardo Lopez is one of the more sought-after producers in Paicol, having won many regional competitions, including the inaugural Copa de Oro. In the cup we find a very expressive Pink Bourbon profile, with excellently articulated acidities of lemon, lime, ripe raspberry, and a hint of florality.

items.title: 2023 Hacienda La Esmeralda; Reina 41S, Gesha - Panama
items.desc: Gesha is a truly special variety; especially from Panama, and especially from this farm. Its flavors are defined, articulated, unique and elegant. This cup is a beautifully integrated experience of intoxicating florals of jasmine and honeysuckle, a crisp citrus acidity, and ripe stone fruit notes.

items.title: 2023 Jose Javier Canacue; El Mirador, Late - Colombia
items.desc: This is a very cool organic Chiroso from Huila. Chiroso has quickly become one of our favorite varieties being cultivated in Colombia, but it is rare to find it outside of Antioquia. In the cup we find lovely tropical fruits, expressive acidities, and a soft florality.

items.title: 2023 Mario Moreno; El Guayabo - Honduras
items.desc: El Guayabo is one of the highest-elevation coffee-producing farms in Santa Bárbara, and consistently produces some of our favorite coffee from Honduras. We look forward to this coffee's arrival each year. In the cup we find melons, redcurrants, and plum.

items.title: 2023 Jamith Burbano; Buena Vista, Late - Colombia
items.desc: Jamith is an inspiring young producer in his second year working with the Monkaaba project, and it is a pleasure to offer his coffee again this year. In the cup we find ripe melon, white grape, and milk chocolate.

items.title: 2023 Duwancho, Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a really lovely honey-processed selection from extreme altitude in Arbegona––one of our favorite growing regions in Ethiopia. In the cup we find a profile of vibrant tropical fruits, herbal tea, and melon.

items.title: 2023 Duwancho, Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a lovely washed selection from extreme altitude in Arbegona—one of our favorite growing regions in Ethiopia. In the cup we find lively acidity, watermelon, honeydew, and jasmine.

items.title: 2023 Kiawamururu - Kenya
items.desc: Our last Kenyan release of the year is an excellent selection from the famous region of Nyeri on the western side of Mount Kenya. In the cup we find a lovely and lively acidity, raspberry tea florality, dark fruits, and a long finish.

items.title: 2023 Amalia Castañeda - Mexico
items.desc: This is a small single-producer lot from the Sierra Mazateca mountains in Oaxaca. We have been exploring this region for the past three years, and it remains one of the most challenging places to work. In the cup we find baking chocolate, strawberry preserves, and honey.

items.title: 2023 Inzá Pink - Colombia
items.desc: This Pink Bourbon separation comes to us from the challenging but exciting region of Cauca. Though traditionally difficult to work in, Cauca can produce remarkable coffee, and we are grateful for the opportunity to work in this unique place. In the cup we find red currant, lime, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2023 Peterson & Purity Muthathai; Ngaratua Estate, AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: Ngaratua consistently produces complex and dynamic profiles, and has quickly become one of our favorite farms to work with in Kenya. This lot is essentially pure SL28, and sings of dark fruits and citrus, with a subtle florality as well.

items.title: 2023 The Lamastus Family; Elida Estate, Mina, Gesha, Natural - Panama
items.desc: Gesha is a truly special variety; especially from Panama, and especially from this farm. This natural-process selection is a much more fruit-forward expression of this variety and terroir. In the cup we find Concord grape juice, ripe mango, and champagne.

items.title: 2023 The Lamastus Family; Elida Estate, Plano, Gesha, Washed - Panama
items.desc: Gesha is a truly special variety; especially from Panama, and especially from this farm. Its flavors are defined, articulated, unique and elegant. This cup is a beautifully integrated experience of intoxicating florals of jasmine and honeysuckle, a crisp citrus acidity, and ripe stone fruit notes.

items.title: 2023 Las Perlitas - Colombia
items.desc: This unique blend is composed of tiny high-quality lots that couldn't be exported on their own because of how small they were. In the cup we find ripe fruits, vibrant acidity, and excellent sweetness.

items.title: 2023 Pedro Moreno; El Mango - Honduras
items.desc: This is our third year working with this micro lot, and it was once again one of the top-scoring lots we tasted on the buying table at San Vicente. This coffee is complex, with notes of sparkling blackcurrant, raspberry, and a long, delicate Earl Grey finish.

items.title: 2023 Guchienda Estate; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: The Guchienda Estate is one of our more exciting projects in Kenya. This year, it won the annual African Taste of Harvest competition! The lot is 100% pure SL28, dynamic and exciting. In the cup we find a classic Kenyan profile of blackberry, hibiscus, and subtle florals.

items.title: 2023 Erick Bravo; Finca El Chaferote, Early - Colombia
items.desc: This is our third season working with the coffees from Erick Bravo, and his Pink Bourbon continues to be one of our favorite expressions of the variety. In the cup we find a classic Pink Bourbon profile of lemonade, ripe stone fruit, and berries.

items.title: 2023 Raul Perez; La Llano, Gesha - Guatemala
items.desc: The variety separations from Raul's inspiring farm provide a special opportunity to taste different varieties grown in the same microclimate. This Gesha separation has a very traditional profile of jasmine, peach, and citrus.

items.title: 2023 Raul Perez; La Llano, H1 Hybrid - Guatemala
items.desc: Raul is one of the few producers we work with who can deliver multiple variety separations from the same farm. This provides a very unique opportunity to taste many different varieties from the same microclimate. In the cup we find a sweetness-focused profile of baking chocolate, cream, and strawberry.

items.title: 2023 Mbature Family; Kamavindi, AB Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is a single-estate AB selection from the Mbature family on the southeastern slopes of Mt. Kenya. Working with this family's coffee is a dream and an honor, as their production and processing are among the best we've ever seen. In the cup we find a very bright profile of red currant, citrus, and plum.

items.title: 2023 Raul Perez; La Llano, Pink Bourbon - Guatemala
items.desc: This is a 100% Pink Bourbon separation from Raul Perez. We've been working with Raul for several years, but this is our first season getting a Pink Bourbon separation. In the cup we find dark fruits, honey, and citrus.

items.title: 2023 Danche, Late - Ethiopia
items.desc: Danche is just a few kilometers from the famed Chelbessa washing station, which regularly produces some of our favorite Ethiopian coffees. In the cup we find intoxicating florals, watermelon, peach, and a lively citrus acidity.

items.title: 2023 Alejandro Renjifo; Reina De Saba, Typica - Colombia
items.desc: 100% Typica is quite rare—especially in Colombia. This particular lot from our dear friend Alejandro Renjifo is exquisite. In the cup we find a very clean and transparent representation of terroir: dark berries, pomegranate, and floral.

items.title: 2023 Alejandro Renjifo; Reina De Saba, Gesha, Late - Colombia
items.desc: This remains one of our favorite Gesha profiles year after year. The seeds were initially hand-selected from a specific Gesha tree in Acevedo and planted high up in San Agustín. In the cup we find intoxicating florals, ripe berries, star fruit, peach, articulated acidity, and a delightful sweetness.

items.title: 2023 Mazateca Mujeres - Mexico
items.desc: This is a combined lot from the gardens of a group of female producers in the mountains of Yoloxochitlán, whose yields aren't independently large enough to mill and export as micro lots. In the cup we find a sweetness-forward profile of dark chocolate, citrus acidity, and strawberry.

items.title: 2023 Japheth Maura; Makena, AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: We are excited to be working with the Makena Estate on the southern slopes of Mt. Kenya for the first time! In the cup we find a lively profile of blackberry, hibiscus, and cranberry.

items.title: 2023 Addisu Kidane; Halo Beriti - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is a super cool single-producer lot from Gedeb. Addisu grows and processes coffee alongside his wife and family. He has been producing sundried naturals for the past five years, but was finally able to build his own wet mill in 2022. In the cup we find berries, nectarine, and coffee blossom.

items.title: DiFluid R2
items.desc:
We have partnered with DiFluid to offer their innovative R2 refractometers.
A refractometer measures the coffee particles in your brew, giving you an objective reading of concentration, strength, and extraction. While cup quality is paramount, the ability to measure extraction is extremely useful for maximizing your brew, and also allows us to more effectively help you troubleshoot from afar.
We have tested these units extensively, and have found them to be intuitive and reliable.
For more information, visit DiFluid's website .
SEY subscribers are eligible for a significant discount on the DiF

items.title: 2023 Banko Gotiti - Ethiopia
items.desc: We've been working in Banko Gotiti for several years now. Coffees from this region are always super clean, bright, and elegant. In this cup we find wildflower honey, tangerine, and apricot.

items.title: 2023 Yeferson Hernández; Los Tabares - Colombia
items.desc: We continue to explore Urrao because we are completely enchanted by Chirosos from this region. Yeferson is a 22-year-old, third-generation producer, and this expressive cup brims with mango and passion fruit, a white peach florality, and exhilarating acidity.

items.title: 2023 Kiandieri; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This is our first time working with this particular cooperative, located on the western border of Kirinyaga––right next to Nyeri. In the cup we find red currant, limeade, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2023 Stefan Muller; Benjie, Gesha - Panama
items.desc: This Gesha separation comes from a very impressive producer. Stefan grows an incredible array of varieties and believes "art exists to express feelings, connect, and identify dreams". In the cup we find a classic Gesha profile of jasmine, honeysuckle, and white peach.

items.title: 2023 Gargari Gutiti - Ethiopia
items.desc: Gargari is located just outside of the town of Gedeb, in a small region that has produced exceptional coffees for a very long time. In this cup we find a sparkling profile of tangerine, jasmine pearls, and lemon.

items.title: 2023 Tasiwa Estate; AA Separation - Kenya
items.desc: This single-estate lot comes from Kiambu, one of our favorite producing regions in the world. In the cup we find blackcurrant, lemonade, and rose.

items.title: 2023 Jose Jaoquin Bolaños; Villa Sophia, Gesha - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year working with Jose Bolaños, and this Gesha separation is remarkably dynamic and complex. In the cup we find a fruit-forward profile of strawberry, nectarine, and jasmine.

items.title: 2023 Paxtle - Mexico
items.desc: This is our second release of the season from the mountains of the Sierra Mazateca. This one comes from a producing group that goes by the name of Paxtle, in San Mateo, on the western side of the valley. In the cup we find a classic Mexican profile of baking chocolate, fresh strawberry, and honey.

items.title: 2023 David Berrio; La Casita, Late - Colombia
items.desc: David Berrio's 1.5 hectare (3.7 acre) garden is by far the most remote site we've worked with in Urrao. This separation is from his late harvest, and sings of ripe tropical fruits with a lively acidity and berry-like complexity.

items.title: 2023 Kubi - Ethiopia
items.desc: This selection comes from a small regional group of producers who deliver to the Chelbessa washing station, which regularly produces some of our favorite Ethiopian coffees. In the cup we find intoxicating florals, watermelon, peach, and a lively citrus acidity.

items.title: 2023 Agustín Roque - Mexico
