items.title: Unwind
items.desc: Enjoy all the flavour without the caffeine. Unwind by ONA Coffee is a smooth, balanced decaf coffee blend—perfect for espresso or milk-based drinks.

items.title: Raspberry Candy
items.desc: Discover Raspberry Candy by ONA Coffee —our most popular, fruit-forward espresso blend with vibrant berry notes and creamy white chocolate sweetness. Designed to shine in milk-based drinks, Raspberry Candy is a playful yet refined coffee experience that has become a favourite for baristas and home brewers alike.

items.title: Maple
items.desc: The maple tree's enduring strength speaks to our commitment to nature and sustainability. Maple was created to be a traditional style milk coffee, perfect for everyday drinking. It is a bold, full-bodied coffee with flavours of caramel, malt, nut and spices.

items.title: Gateway
items.desc: Want an approachable introduction to specialty coffee? If you’re new to coffee or buying beans for someone just starting their journey, our Gateway Coffee is the perfect milk-based coffee blend to ease you in. These coffee beans deliver a sweet, creamy profile with tasting notes of chocolate truffle and mixed berries.

items.title: Aspen
items.desc: An Aspen is a variety of poplar tree that reminds us of where ONA first started. Throwing back to the memories that founder Saša Šestić has of Canberra's poplar-lined roads, as he travelled from roastery to cafe. This full-flavoured blend is decadent and smooth, designed for everyday drinking. It is the perfect coffee for chocolate lovers.

items.title: Haro Wachu
items.desc:
Produced at the Haro Wachu washing station in Uraga, in Ethiopia’s Oromia region, this naturally processed coffee showcases the vibrant character of Ethiopian coffee.
Versatile and enjoyable as both filter and espresso, it offers a rounded mouthfeel with a rich and expressive flavour profile. Expect notes of blueberry, lemon curd, and floral honey, coming together in a beautifully balanced cup.
A great choice for anyone looking to explore the fruity and floral side of Ethiopian coffee.

items.title: Eddy Macdonald
items.desc:
A very limited lot from coffee producer Eddy Macdonald!
This natural Pacamara coffee is harvested at peak maturity and begins drying approximately four hours after harvesting. The first five days of drying take place on a sun patio, where the cherries are turned every hour and exposed to sunlight from 9 AM to 3 PM each day. After this initial period, the cherries are moved to African-style raised beds for an additional 17 days, receiving sunlight from 9 AM to 4 PM, while still being turned every hour. Once drying is complete, the coffee is stored in clean sacks until it reaches our warehouse,

items.title: Oswaldo Toro
items.desc:
Introducing the newest addition to our Competition Category: a natural anaerobic Caturra from Colombia!
Through a carefully controlled fermentation process, this coffee develops a beautifully balanced yet expressive cup, bringing out its naturally exotic and fruity character.
Expect vibrant notes of cassis, bubble gum, and grapefruit, complemented by a distinctive sticky mouthfeel.
Bright, fruity, and full of character, this Caturra is a must-try for adventurous coffee lovers.
Available for both filter and espresso.

items.title: Obeimar Ordóñez
items.desc:
A new addition to our collection of floral coffees: Obeimar Ordóñez from Colombia!
This washed and anaerobically processed coffee delivers an expressive aroma and a delicate, refined cup. Smooth and elegant, it offers a memorable tasting experience without compromising on clarity.
Expect notes of raspberry, violet, and gummy bears, complemented by a smooth mouthfeel. Clean, balanced, and delicate, this coffee beautifully showcases the refined character of the Colombia Castillo variety.

items.title: Gundikhan
items.desc:
For the first time, Indian coffee joins the Manhattan lineup!
Many of you have asked us to bring Indian coffee to Manhattan, but for a long time, we couldn’t find the right coffee to start with. That changed this year, when we tried a lot from Gundikhan Estate and knew we’d found the one.
This yeast-fermented washed coffee brings together the fresh taste of green apple and the gentle sweetness of brown sugar, complemented by the citrusy spice of black lime “loumi” and a sticky, rich, lingering finish.
Available in both espresso and filter roasts.
We’re excited to finally share Indian coffee wi

items.title: Origami Paper Filter S
items.desc:
Looking for the perfect paper filter for your Origami Dripper?
Made specifically for the Origami Dripper, these filters are produced by Cafec Japan, one of Japan’s renowned paper filter manufacturers. Made from high-quality virgin pulp, they are designed to deliver a smooth, stable flow for balanced, even extraction.
The cone-shaped design helps maintain a consistent flow throughout the brewing process, resulting in a clean cup that highlights the natural flavors of your coffee. The bleached white paper is designed to minimize papery taste, allowing the coffee itself to shine.
Available in siz

items.title: Las Marias
items.desc:
Fantastic Wush Wush from José Giraldo!
This exceptional Wush Wush pushes the variety into new territory. An extended anaerobic fermentation amplifies its naturally exotic and floral character, bringing deeper layers of tropical and fermented fruit while preserving its signature aromatic lift.
In the cup, expect vibrant notes of pineapple, orange, and bergamot, complemented by a juicy, refreshing mouthfeel. Intense, complex, and wonderfully expressive, this is a truly experimental Wush Wush that leaves a lasting impression.
Available for both filter and espresso.

items.title: Yilver Pajoy
items.desc:
COPA DE ORO ’25 — 5th Place, Western Division.
We’re delighted to present an extraordinary competition coffee: an award-winning microlot crafted from washed Gesha.
Elegant, expressive, and remarkably refined, this coffee offers the distinctive character we look for in exceptional competition lots.
In the cup, expect delicate notes of yellow plum, fig, and Earl Grey, complemented by a vibrant yet rounded mouthfeel and a beautifully refined sweetness.
A coffee created to stand apart — now available for you to experience.
Enjoy it as filter or espresso.

items.title: Karimikui
items.desc:
We’re excited to announce Karimikui from Kenya is back! Quality control begins with strict hand-sorting of cherries upon delivery.
The cherries are then pulped and undergo an overnight fermentation process in concrete tanks to break down the mucilage.
After fermentation, the coffee is washed and graded by density in clean water channels, followed by a final soak. The parchment is then moved to raised African beds for sun-drying.
The drying stage typically lasts between 7 and 15 days, where the coffee is continuously hand-turned and sorted to ensure uniform moisture content.
To protect the qual

items.title: El Ingenio-Meraki
items.desc:
Attention! This coffee has a sticker on the packaging with a brewing recipe designed exclusively for the Meraki espresso machine.
This coffee is grown at El Ingenio in El Salvador by the Urrutia family.
Once picked, the coffee cherries are transported to San Antonio, the wet mill run by Enrique Urrutia.
At the mill, the cherries pass through a series of depulpers, each calibrated for different levels of ripeness. The first depulper is set specifically for ripe, red cherries. If a cherry isn’t pulped during the first pass, a processing machine known as a criba moves it on to the next depulper.

items.title: Shyira
items.desc:
We’re excited to share another delicious coffee from Rwanda! The Shyira coffee is named after the Shyira Coffee Washing Station, which showcases the resilience and potential of coffee farming in Nyabihu. This region is known for producing some of Rwanda’s most unique and sought-after specialty coffees.
These washed Red Bourbon coffeebeans, is grown in the high mountains at an elevation of 1,850 to 2,300 meters above sea level. Nyabihu, often referred to as the “place of darkness,” earned its name due to its frequent heavy cloud cover and intense rainy seasons.
You can expect tasting notes of s

items.title: Ruronzi
items.desc:
We’re excited to welcome another exceptional Rwandan coffee to our lineup. This coffee is processed as a Natural with 120 hours of anaerobic fermentation, where temperature, pH, and microbial activity are carefully controlled to shape its unique character.
After fermentation, the cherries are slowly dried on raised beds to preserve the complex aromatic compounds developed during processing.
The result is a vibrant and expressive coffee with intense fruit aromatics, refined sweetness, and a clean, well-structured cup.
Expect blueberry, melon, and cherry with a juicy mouthfeel in your cup!

items.title: El Ingenio
items.desc:
This coffee is grown at El Ingenio in El Salvador by the Urrutia family.
Once picked, the coffee cherries are transported to San Antonio, the wet mill run by Enrique Urrutia.
At the mill, the cherries pass through a series of depulpers, each calibrated for different levels of ripeness. The first depulper is set specifically for ripe, red cherries. If a cherry isn’t pulped during the first pass, a processing machine known as a criba moves it on to the next depulper. With four depulping lines available, this system allows the mill to carefully separate and prioritise the highest-quality cherries

items.title: Jose Antonio Cenon
items.desc:
We are excited to present an extraordinary coffee: COPA DE ORO ‘25 — 5th Place, Central Division.
This award-winning microlot, predominantly made from washed Gesha, delivers a beautifully expressive and refined cup.
As a competition coffee, it boasts remarkable character and is now available for you to enjoy.
In the cup, you will find notes of rose lemonade, orange, and papaya, balanced by a vibrant, juicy mouthfeel and refined sweetness.
Experience it now as either a filter coffee or an espresso.

items.title: De Nieuwe Barista (Dutch language)
items.desc:
A Deep Journey Through the World of Coffee
Written by coffee experts and multiple champions Rose van Asten and Wendelien van Bunnik, De Nieuwe Barista takes you on a complete journey from bean to cup.
Blending accessibility with depth, the book covers everything from tasting and brewing methods to technique and extraction. Rather than focusing on theory, it offers practical insights, clear explanations, and real-world examples drawn from modern coffee practice.
Whether you’re an enthusiastic home brewer or an ambitious professional, this book is an essential guide to refining your skills and b

items.title: Bombe
items.desc:
We’re excited to welcome another exceptional Ethiopian coffee to our lineup.
This naturally processed lot from Daye Bensa Coffee, produced by Assefa and Mulugeta Dukamo, showcases everything we love about high-elevation Sidama coffees — clarity, elegance, and vibrant fruit character.
In the cup, expect a memorable profile of yellow raspberry, rose, and bergamot, combining juicy sweetness with delicate florals and a refined citrus lift.
Versatile and expressive, this coffee shines beautifully as both filter and espresso—choose your preferred brew method and enjoy.

items.title: Sweet Valley-Meraki
items.desc:
Attention! This coffee has a sticker on the packaging with a brewing recipe designed exclusively for the Meraki espresso machine.
This coffee was originally discontinued, but in collaboration with CGLE we were able to help revive this coffee and redevelop the processing and production to bring it back to life, exclusively for us!
For those new to this coffee, it is a naturally processed Colombia varietal coming from the Potosi farm at the famous Cafe Granja La Esparanza.
The Colombia coffee varietal is a hybrid of Caturra and the infamous Hybrido de Timor, a hugely influential cross between Ar

items.title: Shoondhisa-Meraki
notes: A hint of white sugar sweetness
items.desc:
Attention! This coffee has a sticker on the packaging with a brewing recipe designed exclusively for the Meraki espresso machine.
Shoondhisa: A Guji Gem for Every Coffee Lover
Introducing Shoondhisa, a standout coffee from Guji known for its natural processing and versatile flavor. Whether brewed as filter coffee or espresso, Shoondhisa delivers a round mouthfeel with rich notes of berry compote, strawberry juice, and a hint of white sugar sweetness. Perfect for any coffee lover.

items.title: Viani-Meraki
items.desc:
Attention! This coffee has a sticker on the packaging with a brewing recipe designed exclusively for the Meraki espresso machine.
Viani has a special place in our hearts here at MCR as it’s a coffee that has been on our list since we started Manhattan Coffee Roasters.
The co-operative at Viani produce an old world and typical profile. It’s big, rich and has just a slight bit of acidity that’s perfect for anyone that wants an intense flavour experience from a coffee.

items.title: City Limits-Meraki
items.desc:
Attention! This coffee has a sticker on the packaging with a brewing recipe designed exclusively for the Meraki espresso machine.
City Limits was created as a year-round espresso blend that delivers a perfectly balanced, sweet cup. It’s designed to shine in milk-based drinks while also offering enough complexity to be enjoyed on its own.
Our mission has always been to keep the blend consistent and fresh by featuring high-quality, in-season green coffee. This version features a 66/34 blend of Brazil Inacio Soares F2 and El Ingenio from El Salvador.
What makes this version special is that City L

items.title: Brooklyn-Meraki
items.desc:
Attention! This coffee has a sticker on the packaging with a brewing recipe designed exclusively for the Meraki espresso machine.
Introducing the Brooklyn Blend: a balanced fusion of 90% Brazil Inacio Soares F2 and 10% Panamanian Geisha from Finca Santa Teresa. This blend combines the richness of Brazilian coffee with the elegance of Geisha, offering smooth notes of candied orange, praline, cream and a juicy mouthfeel.

items.title: El Paseo
items.desc:
El Paseo is our newest coffee in the Exceptional category.
Produced by Huver Castillo in Nariño, Colombia, this Caturra lot begins with the careful selection of fully ripe cherries. The coffee undergoes a 36-hour pre-fermentation in cherry, followed by floating and disinfection using a sea salt solution (2%). It is then transferred to stainless steel tanks for controlled anaerobic fermentation, where the coffee ferments for six days. During this stage, collected leachates and specific enzymes are added to promote a distinctive floral profile.
After fermentation, the coffee is mechanically drie

items.title: Fredy Orantes
items.desc:
We’re excited to introduce this Natural Pacamara from Fredy Orantes!
Fredy Orantes is a prominent coffee grower in Santa Rosa, known for his dedicated work to uphold high standards in both cultivation and harvesting to produce exceptional coffees.
After a meticulous picking process where workers select only the ripest cherries, the coffee is placed in clean sacks for approximately 48 hours of fermentation. Once this fermentation period is complete, Fredy moves the coffee to raised beds that are strategically positioned to take advantage of the abundant sunlight in Fraijanes. The coffee dries o

items.title: Rainbow
items.desc:
Welcome back, Rainbow!
A true fan favorite, Rainbow is finally back! You’ve been asking for its return through messages and emails almost every day, and we’re so excited to share a fresh batch with you.
This vibrant anaerobic Pink Bourbon bursts with an explosive fruit-forward profile, bringing a playful mix of papaya, strawberry, and dragon fruit. With its juicy finish and expressive aromas, Rainbow shines in both filter and espresso.
Bright, juicy, and full of character — this is one comeback you don’t want to miss!

items.title: Sweet Valley
items.desc:
This coffee was originally discontinued, but in collaboration with CGLE we were able to help revive this coffee and redevelop the processing and production to bring it back to life, exclusively for us!
For those new to this coffee, it is a naturally processed Colombia varietal coming from the Potosi farm at the famous Cafe Granja La Esparanza.
The Colombia coffee varietal is a hybrid of Caturra and the infamous Hybrido de Timor, a hugely influential cross between Arabica and Robusta that brings a lot of disease resistant traits to Arabica. By crossing with Caturra, members of Cenicafe, the Col

items.title: Shoondhisa Anaerobic
items.desc:
We’re so excited to release another Ethiopian coffee from the one and only “King of Guji” — Ture Waji!
Same variety, completely different processing, and a whole new experience in your morning cup.
This lot underwent an initial fermentation in plastic barrels for 48 hours before being dried on raised beds, just like a traditional natural, for 15–20 days.
Expect vibrant notes of blueberry, orange, and pink Fruittella, with a juicy, fruit-forward mouthfeel.
Another beautiful expression of Guji, showcasing just how much processing can transform the character of the same variety.

items.title: El Vergel Decaf
items.desc:
El Vergel Decaf Is Back!
Experience the exceptional taste of El Vergel Decaf, processed using the EA Sugarcane Decaffeination Method. This natural decaffeination process is free from synthetic chemicals and carefully preserves the coffee’s original character, allowing the beans to retain their full aroma, sweetness, and flavor complexity.
Produced from Red and Yellow Caturra varieties, this coffee offers a delicious flavor profile of sweet baked apple, prunes, and dark chocolate, complemented by a silky, smooth mouthfeel.
The EA Sugarcane process is renowned for delivering a clean, safe, and f

items.title: City Limits
items.desc:
City Limits was created as a year-round espresso blend that delivers a perfectly balanced, sweet cup. It’s designed to shine in milk-based drinks while also offering enough complexity to be enjoyed on its own.
Our mission has always been to keep the blend consistent and fresh by featuring high-quality, in-season green coffee. This version features a 66/34 blend of Brazil Inacio Soares F2 and El Ingenio from El Salvador.

Viani has a special place in our hearts here at MCR as it’s a coffee that has been on our list since we started Manhattan Coffee Roasters.
The co-operative at Viani produce an old world and typical profile. It’s big, rich and has just a slight bit of acidity that’s perfect for anyone that wants an intense flavour experience from a coffee.

Perfect for any coffee lover.

But I guess they’re also different, because I can’t drink music and I usually don’t dance to coffee. What would decaf music be? Probably the Wii sports theme.
Anyways, back to the funk. Negele Gorbitu is back, baby! A long time favorite here at Friedhats, beloved for being a great showing of what we think anaerobic coffees should taste like- complexity, long sweetness, and of course, some delightful funk. I think if the Negele Gorbitu was a so

items.title: Ethiopia Bogalech Dukalee Natural
items.desc:
The familiar Bogalech Dukallee comes via the Sookoo producers, who also produce the Bookkisa that we all love so much. This coffee was farmed by Bogalech Dukkale, who after inheriting her family’s farm in Guji took over the reins and has been producing high quality coffees since. Coming from a family of coffee producers means a long history of understanding what works and how the landscape and environment is ever changing, and there are certainly lots which we have that echo that knowledge - this is one of them.

items.title: Honey Melon
items.desc: Honey Melon is our latest Indonesian coffee from Frinsa Collective in West Java, produced by a community of smallholder farmers working with Wildan Mustofa and Atieq Mustikaningtyas. This lot undergoes a honey-lactic process, with a controlled fermentation using Lactobacillus. The cup is fruity and sweet, with notes of melon, grapefruit and orange, bringing together a nice balance of sweetness and citrus acidity.

items.title: Pillow Talk
items.desc: Los Nogales does decaf a little differently. This Caturra is grown, processed and decaffeinated at the farm in Pitalito, giving Oscar Hernandez and his team control over the coffee from cherry to finished decaf. It’s bright and sweet, with starfruit, agave and rosemary. A decaf we’d happily drink whether we were looking for one or not. * Due to the decaffeination process, the beans may have an unusual colour. This is completely normal and does not affect the quality of the coffee.

items.title: Peachy Daze
items.desc: Peachy Daze is back, a clean washed Ethiopian from the Chelbesa washing station in Gedeb, where heirloom varieties grow at 2173 masl. The cup is light and delicate, with white peach and lemon up front, black tea through the middle and a soft elderflower finish.

items.title: Blackberry Dust
items.desc: Blackberry Dust is a late-harvest natural Ethiopian coffee from the Buku Abel washing station in Guji, which arrived in Europe just a few weeks ago. Around 400 smallholder farmers contribute to the station, growing heirloom varieties at elevations between 1,900 and 2,100 masl. The cup is fruity and sweet, with notes of blackberry, wild strawberry and blueberry yoghurt, followed by a soft, creamy finish.

items.title: Macaron
items.desc: One of our all-time favourites from Johan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, this natural Red Bourbon has become one of those coffees we’re always excited to bring back. It goes through an advanced anaerobic natural process and comes out big, juicy and seriously sweet, with strawberry jam, raspberry macaron and buttercream.

items.title: Sticky Pudding
items.desc: Our Christmas coffee is here! This year we’ve worked with CATA Export in Colombia to create something inspired by the festive season. This bourbon undergoes a co-fermentation with cinnamon, cardamom, mandarin and cherry, giving it a distinctive profile while keeping plenty of sweetness in the cup. Expect notes of cinnamon, cardamom and fresh fir – a very festive profile.

items.title: Cream Donut
items.desc: Cream Donut is a collaboration with Cata Export and producer Franky Hoyos in Colombia. A yeast-inoculated natural Caturra Chiroso developed for DAK through rounds of back-and-forth trialling. It’s an unusual coffee that has somehow become one of our staples and a bestseller, loved for its distinct character and the ridiculously good flat white it makes. Expect chocolate milk, cherry-filled doughnut and vanilla, whether you brew it as filter or espresso.

items.title: Plum Butter
items.desc: Plum Butter is a natural from Bulambuli in East Uganda, produced with our long-time partners at Ibero. It’s a profile we don’t come across often from Uganda: deep, smooth and fruit-forward, with dark plum, grape cordial and cacao. Rich without becoming too heavy.

items.title: Berry Blues
items.desc: Berry Blues is back. We’ve had this coffee in different variations over the years, sometimes under Berry Blues, sometimes as Blueberry Boom, and it remains a favourite across the DAK team for its big fruit character and how much fun it is to drink. This year’s harvest from Esayas Beriso is an anaerobic natural, grown high in Oromia, Ethiopia, and slowly dried in the shade. There’s plenty of dark fruit and a boozy edge: grape soda up front, myrtle liquor behind it, and a cashew-butter richness that gives the cup its buttery body and creamy mouthfeel.

items.title: Darling
items.desc: Darling comes from Danche Washing Station in Gedeb, and it’s one of the more delicate Ethiopians we’ve had this year. The coffee goes through a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation before being washed, resulting in a cup with good clarity despite the additional fermentation. Wild florals lead, followed by peach iced tea and a black-tea finish. Light, elegant and very tea-like.

items.title: Rhubarb Fizz
items.desc: Our next Kenyan of the season, and one of our favourites this year. Rhubarb Fizz is a washed AA from Ndimi Factory in Kirinyaga, bringing together SL28, SL34, Batian and Ruiru 11 from the surrounding smallholder farms. Juicy and layered, with rhubarb soda, blackcurrant and orange.

items.title: Hazel Nuts
items.desc: Hazel Nuts is a natural Catuaí from Chinacla in the Marcala region of Honduras, grown by our longtime partners Marysabel Caballero and Moises Herrera. We’ve been buying their coffees for years, and this is one we particularly like for espresso. Round and silky, with hazelnut, cacao nibs and blackberry, plus a touch of booziness that we really enjoy. Especially good with milk.

items.title: Mango Tango
items.desc: Mango Tango is our next natural Ethiopian of the year, produced by Danche, one of our favourite washing stations this season. We keep coming back to their coffees for how expressive and fruity they can be while still staying remarkably clean. This one is all mango, strawberry candy and mandarin, with good clarity and structure in the cup.

items.title: Silky Way
items.desc: Silky Way is another coffee from Jhoan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, the same family behind Macaron. This time it’s their washed Pink Bourbon, with a completely different side of the farm showing up in the cup. Lemongrass, white florals and crisp green apple, with a bright, sparkling quality that suits the name pretty well.

items.title: Dak x Maison Deux Blanket
items.desc:
For our sixth anniversary, we wanted DAK to step off the coffee box and onto a new medium, so we teamed up with Maison Deux, the Amsterdam-based textile brand founded by Pia and Woes Weinberg.
Together, we made a jacquard-woven blanket from 100% New Zealand wool, featuring an original artwork by Montréal-based artist Valéry Lemay. Warm, weighty and soft, it was first made for our showroom and is now available online in limited quantities.
FROM MAKER TO HAND
The blanket is jacquard-woven from 100% New Zealand wool, meaning the artwork is woven directly into the textile rather than printed onto

items.title: Poppy Soda
items.desc: Poppy Soda is a Pink Bourbon from Sebastián Ramírez at El Placer in Quindío, Colombia. It goes through a pretty elaborate washed process, but the cup itself is all about clarity. Lemonade, jasmine tea and ripe peach, with a bright, almost soda-like quality that makes the name make sense.

items.title: Lemon Spritz
items.desc: Lemon Spritz is a washed Ethiopian from Lalesa washing station in Gedeb, sourced through Nordic Approach. It’s the kind of washed Ethiopian we love to have around: very clean and bright, but still with plenty going on. Lemon peel and florals lead, with a long, structured finish.

items.title: Jazz fruits
items.desc: Jazz Fruits is a staple in our lineup and one we try to keep around all year, whenever the harvest allows. We source this community lot from Daye Bensa each year for its fruity, easy-going profile and how well it works as espresso, especially with milk. Strawberry, white chocolate and mandarin in the cup. Named after the Jazz Fruits playlists on Spotify.

items.title: Mucho Berry Blend
items.desc:
Mucho Berry
Momos Coffee’s fourth signature blend
Ethiopia is widely known as one of the coffee-growing regions loved by many people. In particular, Ethiopian coffees processed by the natural method are recognized for their diverse berry-like aromas and their broad appeal, making them enjoyable for a wide range of drinkers.
Inspired by these berry characteristics, the fourth signature blend, Mucho Berry, was created to express rich and attractive berry-forward aromas.

items.title: Fruity Bonbon Blend
items.desc:
Fruity Bonbon
Momos Coffee’s second signature blend
In 2009, when specialty coffee was first encountered in the United States, coffees with bright acidity and fruit-like aromas were still unfamiliar to many people. However, drawn to the diverse aromas and new flavors found in high-quality coffee, Momos Coffee introduced its second signature blend, Fruity Bonbon, to share the distinct character and appeal of specialty coffee.

items.title: Helfezi Grinding Discs 80mm TDC
items.desc: Built for grinders that demand performance and durability, the Helfezi TDC 80mm burrs deliver exceptional longevity and precision. Rated for up to 8,500 kg of coffee, they outperform standard OEM steel burrs, which typically last just 1,500 kg. With a cost of $1399 compared to $650 for OEM burrs, the Helfezi TDC dramatically lowers your grinding cost per kg—cutting your burr replacement costs by up to 60%. Engineered with advanced surface treatments and optimized cutting geometry, these burrs provide consistent grind quality, reduced heat transfer, and improved resistance to wear and cracking.

items.title: Helfezi Grinding Discs 98mm Alinox
items.desc: These Swiss-made 98mm Alinox coated burrs for EK43/S grinders offer a cost-effective alternative to OEM options, combining certified food and medical-grade coating with advanced geometry to deliver faster grinding, improved flavor clarity, reduced heat, and a cleaner taste, while lasting up to seven times longer than standard steel burrs and supporting multiple grind profiles without seasoning, ultimately helping cafés and roasters significantly reduce maintenance and replacement costs.

items.title: Apax Lab - Jamm
items.desc:
JAMM is formulated to bring roundness and will accentuate the lingering sweetness and creamy mouthfeel of your brew. With just a few drops, it enhances body and softens sharp edges, delivering a smooth and full-flavoured cup.
Used by World Coffee Champions and trusted by leading cafés worldwide , JAMM is the go-to profile for coffee enthusiasts looking to balance complex or funky coffees with ease.
Enhances body and mouthfeel
Increases sweetness and balance
Smooths sharp or funky notes
Perfect for naturals, experimental fermentations, and winey coffees

items.title: Apax Lab - Lylac
items.desc:
LYLAC is designed to extend the finish and highlight delicate aromatics in your coffee. It refines texture, reduces dryness, and reveals a silky, elegant cup with a long, clean aftertaste.
Favoured by coffee competitors and leading cafés worldwide , LYLAC is the secret weapon for showcasing refined coffees and elegant filter brews.
Highlights floral aromatics
Creates a silky, elegant mouthfeel
Extends and cleans the finish
Reduces dryness in lighter profiles

items.title: Apax Lab - Tonik
items.desc:
TONIK is formulated to enhance the vibrant acidity and bring a crisp, juicy kick to your brews. With just a few drops, you can unlock brightness and clarity that make washed coffees and lively fruit-forward profiles shine.
Trusted by over 200 National Champions and 90% of competitors at the 2025 World Brewers Cup , TONIK is a proven tool for baristas, cafés, and home brewers worldwide.
Elevates acidity, vibrancy, and clarity
Adds a lively, juicy character to your coffee
Easy to use in cafés, competitions, or at home
Perfect for washed coffees and fruit-driven profiles

This semi-washed pink bourbon from Finca Buena Vista, run by husband and wife Edgar Motta and Susana Mences, just landed at the roastery! Cherries were picked based on density, depulped, and processed using a semi-washed protocol preserving part of the mucilage. The coffee dried on raised beds in a single layer for 16-22 days.
We are tasting berries and citrus with a sparkling acidity and a slight savory quality.
We score this lot 87.25
Process: Semi-washed
Region: Huila, Colombia
Variety: Pink Bourbon

items.title: Habtamu Guji G1
items.desc:
Habtamu's name has graced our menu all season, and this latest washed Guji is a limited lot with beautiful flavors of cranberry, rhubarb, and peach syrup. Perhaps half a dozen Ethiopian coffees we have this year are attributed to him, and we hope you're enjoying this bull market of washed Ethiopian gems along with us. This coffee went to our subscribers first in August, and we have a limited supply of rested coffee from August 27 ready for immediate shipping!

items.desc:
Roasted just a touch darker than our filter version , this espresso roast makes fantastic straight shots and Americanos.
This is the year of Habtamu! We roasted this gorgeous washed Ethiopian for our monthly subscribers in July, and now it's available for everyone. Ethiopia is having a banner year, and Habtamu is knocking it out of the park. We're loving this coffee's big, ripe apricot coupled with a touch of pineapple and jasmine-like florals.

items.title: Mulu Espresso
items.desc:
Mulu Espresso is Prodigal's new seasonal blend, composed of 100% fresh Ethiopian washed & natural coffees, roasted just a touch darker for espresso. This is a super fun coffee, combining everything we love about classic Ethiopian flavors. Look for citrus and florals from the washed component and rich cherry flavor from the natural. Mulu is punchy and ripe and makes great straight espresso and americanos.

items.title: Finca El Tabor
items.desc:
Finca El Tabor has graced our menu numerous times over the years, and we are excited to present this lot produced by Cesar Dario, son of past menu star Fabiola Ortega. This washed sidra has lovely red winey flavors of grape and cherry, with just a touch of process flavor. This coffee went out to our monthly subscribers first in August, and now it's available to everyone!
Finca El Tabor has been a family endeavor for more than thirty years, spearheaded by Fabiola an her husband Julio Alberto. The farm spans fifteen hectares, with five in coffee production. Cesar plans to expand their already lo

items.title: Zuria Blend
items.desc:
Zuria is Prodigal's new seasonal blend, composed of fresh Ethiopian washed & natural coffees along with Colombian washed chiroso. The washed Ethiopian brings elegant, subtle fruit notes, while the natural brings the tropical fruit punch. The Colombian Chiroso, a darling variety quickly gaining notoriety, brings a bit more fruitiness and balance. This is a zesty blend with big, bold flavors of concord grape, plum and apricot.
Over numerous cuppings, we painstakingly crafted this blend, landing in our goldilocks zone for flavor. We think well-crafted blends are better than the sum of their parts

items.title: Las Virginias — 2026 Cup of Excellence Honduras #4
items.desc: Prodigal is absolutely thrilled to share this 2026 Honduras Cup of Excellence winning coffee! We were bowled over by the ripe, intense flavors of mango, rhubarb, and rum-raisin. Rising Honduran coffee star Fabio Antonio Caballero is making waves in specialty coffee. This gorgeous lot from his Las Virginias farm is the #4 winner of the Exotic category in the 2026 Cup of Excellence auction. Having just started his coffee farming efforts in 2020, he has gone on to win four COE auctions — this coffee and three others from his farm La Salvaje. items.title: Komothai AB
items.desc:
Komothai AB is a fresh crop Kenyan coffee that recently landed in the roastery. The arrival material barely missed Prodigal's strict cupping threshold, so we're selling it as green instead. This coffee features flavors of orange and cherry, and a bit of the typical Kenyan savoriness. We scored it approximately 87 points.
This is a single-estate coffee, which is rare for Kenya. The coffee was also processed and milled on site at the farm, with full traceability beyond the co-op level.

items.title: El Ajial — Freezer Reserve
items.desc:
It's back! 2025's El Ajial caturra was a delicious coffee, and we're cracking open our precious freezer reserve to share this limited supply.
From 2025: El Ajial is a goldilocks coffee that has just the right amount of everything: a little tart cranberry, juicy citrus, and ripe stone fruit.
El Ajial is a very special oasis located high in the Nariño region. Spanning just three hectares, Luis Alfredo Lopez inherited the land in the early 2000's from his father (and first coffee mentor). With the help of his wife and community, they use one hectare solely to produce specialty coffee. The other t

items.title: Nensebo G1
items.desc:
The coffee so nice we released it thrice — Nensebo's back! We sold out in June, and now just a few weeks later we received our final resupply. This blueberry-forward natural Ethiopian is very clean, well-fruited, and aromatic. Also available as espresso!
Nensebo G1 is special because it traces back to just one farm in West Arsi. This is a new relationship for us, and we hope to feature many more coffees from future harvests. This coffee was naturally processed - ripe cherries were picked and then dried on raised beds for two weeks. After that, the coffee was milled, sorted by machine and then

items.title: WATER FOR COFFEE 2nd EDITION
items.desc:
Water for Coffee, 2nd Edition by Maxwell Dashwood and Christopher H. Hendon
Water can transform the character of a coffee. It can accentuate its acidity, or wipe it out entirely. It can increase or decrease body, and alter extraction. It affects the way we roast and the way we brew.
Why? Chemistry, and a little bit of physics.
This book explores the chemistry of water and the effect it has on coffee. Maxwell Colonna-Dashwood and Christopher H. Hendon, chemist, equip you with the tools to allow you to predict - with a given water - how a coffee will taste.

items.title: Flat Bottom Paper Filters
items.desc:
These flat bottom paper filters are XBloom branded but work perfectly in Kalita 155, Orea, etc. They flow identically to more expensive branded filters as well.
These filters also fit the Fellow Stagg but are best suited to smaller doses due to the filter height in the Stagg.
Order along with roasted coffee to save on shipping!
Each pack contains 100 filters.

items.title: Ceado Hoop Brewer & Filters
items.desc:
Don’t let its simplicity fool you. The Ceado Hoop is an amazing brewer.
The Hoop has every attribute of a great manual dripper:
Requires little-to-no skill
Requires little barista attention (this is especially valuable to cafes)
Offers low risk of astringency
Makes even extractions easy to produce
Offers almost automatic consistency
Just pour the water in the outer ring, walk away, and 3–4 minutes later, you have incredible filter coffee.
Like the Pulsar, Tricolate, and Filter3, The Hoop is a no-bypass brewer, which means astringency is easy to avoid, and The Hoop produces high extractions usi

items.title: THE PHYSICS OF ESPRESSO
items.desc:
The Physics of Espresso by Jonathan Gagné is the new standard for espresso science, and will be for generations to come. POE is the modern successor to Espresso Coffee: The Science of Quality by Illy, but with far more actionable advice.
The Physics of Espresso is clear, concise, and comprehensive all at once, as Jonathan guides the reader through the physics of espresso preparation and extraction. Using a blend of published science papers, personal experiments, and some impressive work by other coffee enthusiasts, Jonathan covers every important detail of espresso making, and offers many orig

items.title: THE PHYSICS OF FILTER COFFEE
items.desc:
The Physics of Filter Coffee by astrophysicist Jonathan Gagné is perhaps the most significant book ever written on the science of coffee brewing. In the book Jonathan discusses the physics of percolation, extraction, and grinding, as well as water chemistry. He takes the reader down such rabbit holes as pouring-kettle design, optimizing turbulence while pouring, the impact of fines on percolation, the physics of paper filters, and the geometry of various brewers. He also presents some original ideas about coffee brewing and backs it all up with reams of facts and data.
The most wonderful thing

items.title: WORLD ATLAS OF COFFEE
items.desc: The World Atlas of Coffee is our favorite all-around book about coffee. James Hoffmann is a master communicator, and he does a wonderful job of discussing coffee growing, roasting, and brewing in plain terms anyone can understand, while offering enough detail to maintain the attention of even a seasoned coffee professional. The second half of the book is a tour of coffee-growing regions, with again just the right amount of detail to engage any type of reader. We can’t recommend this book enough for anyone who loves coffee and wants to learn more about it.

items.title: THE COFFEE ROASTERS COMPANION
items.desc: The Coffee Roaster's Companion is the world's first professional-level how-to book about coffee roasting. Scott Rao has been a roaster for over two decades and has consulted for hundreds of the world's finest roasters, using over 250 roasting machines in his career. Scott has put his expertise into this book to help educate roasters everywhere. No serious coffee roaster should go without this book.

items.title: DEAR COFFEE BUYER
items.desc:
Dear Coffee Buyer by Ryan Brown is the first ever book dedicated to the profession of green coffee buying. Brown's vivid descriptions and engaging prose make readers feel like they’re right there with him: tagging along to taste hundreds of coffee samples during a twenty-hour stop in Guatemala, feeling his nervous excitement when he takes a spontaneous buying trip to Honduras with little more than a backpack, and sharing his frustration and determination to find farmers and exporters willing to offer exceptional coffees.
Along the way, Brown takes an in-depth look at coffee bean varieties, pro

items.title: EVERYTHING BUT ESPRESSO
items.desc:
Scott's second book covers all of the major non-espresso forms of coffee brewing. Broken up into three parts, Everything but Espresso covers the following:
Part One - Coffee extraction, extraction measurement, and how to manipulate flavor by changing brewing parameters
Part Two - How to optimize various brewing methods, such as drip, pour over, press pot, and vacuum pot.
Part Three - Proper water chemistry and bean storage.
If you're either an espresso aficionado who wants to spread their wings or someone who cherishes their old press pot, this book is the definitive guide to making the best p

items.title: COFFEE ROASTING BEST PRACTICES
items.desc: Coffee Roasting: Best Practices is the culmination of Scott's 25 years roasting and consulting. It's the most advanced guide ever written about expert-level coffee roasting. There is little overlap with The Coffee Roaster's Companion, which focused on the basics of roasting and different roasting machines. CR:BP focuses solely on advanced techniques to craft and control roast curves, with numerous pages devoted to strategies to avoid "ROR" crashes and flicks, baked coffee, unnecessary roasty-ness, and other roast defects. This book sets the standard for third-wave coffee roasting methodology.

items.title: TERROIR
items.desc:
Terroir is a beautiful book put together by the Barista Hustle about how terroir affects the character of coffee and the success of a crop. The book includes gorgeous photography and interviews with experts such as Tim Wendelboe, Hanna Neuschwander, Willem Boot, Graciano Cruz, and Anabella Meneses.
Terroir offers an incredible education about what contributes to the success and failure of a coffee crop, including farming techniques, soil management, coffee-tree diseases, and the effects of climate change.
If you care about the factors you can control and the steps you can take to support a sus

items.title: THE BUSINESS OF SPECIALTY COFFEE
items.desc:
When Maxwell sent Scott a draft of The Business of Specialty Coffee , he immediately knew it was a winner. Whether you want to get into the coffee business one day or have been in it for many years, there is something in this book for you. The Business of Specialty Coffee is packed with information like no other book on the subject has ever been.
After a short overview to the specialty coffee industry, Maxwell dives into the basics of operating a coffee business, including discussions of margin, risk, scaling, valuation, and access to investment money.
Marketing, market forces, branding, strat

items.title: Iced Coffee - 2.5 Kilos
items.desc:
Prodigal's iced coffee is roasted "omni" style, lighter than our espresso and darker than our filter.
Our iced coffee is always made from recent menu items, so it's an ever-changing offering. Currently composed mostly of a new-crop coffee from Colombia.

items.title: Milk Blend Espresso
items.desc:
This is our signature Milk Blend, composed primarily of a clean, soft Colombian caturra, blended with something a little more sparkly to keep things interesting. The second component changes regularly as we rotate quickly through fresh green coffee, but this blend remains consistent and always optimized for milk drinks.
Make sure to check that the roast date you've selected is what you're looking for — The UPCOMING ROAST date is listed under the tasting notes at the top of this product page, or shop from our rested selection if available!
Please read our shipping info page!

items.title: Boulder Blend
items.desc:
We love blending coffees. By selectively combining washed and natural/honey-processed coffees, Boulder Blend unites ripe and fruity flavors with clean, juicy qualities.
We don’t buy coffees specifically for blending. Instead, we craft every batch of Boulder Blend from our limited headline coffees.
Boulder Blend’s components may change slightly week to week, but it's always fruity, bright and balanced — a coffee you'll reach for every day.
Process: primarily washed, with some anaerobic, natural, or honey
Region: global
Variety: mixed
Roast level: Filter/Omni Roast

items.title: First Batch 1 Kilo
items.desc:
This one-kilogram bag of coffee is from the first roast batch of a new coffee. Subsequent batches improve, but the first batch is still delicious. We price this bag to reflect that.
First Batch is an ever changing coffee, so you may receive any one or a blend of our coffees, a surprise every time! And though you may want the details of what's in this blend, week-to-week we don't keep track, opting to spend less on logistical hours and instead passing the savings on to you! For traceability, check out our non-blend offerings :)
First Batch is currently a super-limited, one-per-customer offering

items.title: Hanan Million Natural | Guji, Ethiopia
items.desc:
Local landrace varieties carrying the particular character of Buku Hambella. Hanan founded ASHKIM with her mother, Asha Yuya, the name honouring Asha and her sister Kimiya.
The fermentation that happens inside a drying coffee fruit is microbially complex and environmentally responsive, and the difference between a natural that sings and one that doesn't comes down to decisions made on the drying bed across weeks. Hanan's lands in the expressive register: purple haribo gummies, bubblegum, white tea are things we’ve been picking up with this one.

items.title: Moata Raya Lunar Honey | Agaro, Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot is a fun experiment using 74110 local landrace (and catalogued by JARC) grown by smallholder farmers on garden plots in Agaro. Moata bought this fruit from locals as he doesn't have a farm, but he still wanted to work through this processing idea - and we get to enjoy the results together. This lot is a honey, where Moata used a hand disk pulper with no further soak, and laid the parchment out on raised beds, covered with shade mesh during the day, and opening the netting at dusk and overnight, resulting in things like nougaty white mulberry, taffy and oolong.

items.title: Basha Bekele Natural (minis) | Sidama, Ethiopia
items.desc: Variety 74158 grown by 1st place COE winner (2024), Basha Bekele, on his farm in Bombe, Bensa, Sidama. Proccessed as a natural with whole fruit dried on raised beds. This lot is particularily special as it features the smallest screen sizes, not normally exportable. Moata, who works with Crop to Cup took it upon himself to painstakingly re-sort these 'minis', with the idea that these smaller fruits have outsized flavour. We're inclined to agree.

items.title: Duromina (JARC landraces) | Agaro, Ethiopia
items.desc: Semi-wild local landraces grown in the forests of Agaro, Ethiopia. Picked by smallholders who deliver to Duromina washing station to be processed. Mechanically demucilaged using water conserving Penagos system & dried on raised beds. This lower intervention process (recently being referred to as "zero-fermentation") results in bright florals, malted-milk candies, & oolong.

items.title: Marlon Bolaños (Ají Washed) | Huila, Colombia
items.desc: Ají from Marlon Bolaños' farm, The Three Brothers which he manages with his two brothers, Hemerson & Pedro in Acevedo, Huila. Though a relatively low intervention process with a short 12hr. fermentation time, the resulting profile is notably fruity with flavours of cream soda, pineapple and sage.

items.title: Habtamu Fikadu - Chelbesa site (Kurume, Dega & Wolisho) | Gedeb, Ethiopia
items.desc:
Kurume, Dega, & Wolisho varieties grown by smallholder farmers on garden plots in Chelbesa, Gedeb, Ethiopia and delivered to the Chelbesa washing station (owned by Habtamu Fikadu Aga and his company Kuri Mountain Coffee) to be processed. Processed as a traditional washed, submerged fermentation in tanks before being washed & dried on raised beds, creating an articulate classic profile we love, juicy & bright, like white champagne peach, floral honey, and sencha tea-like qualities.
Featured in our October 2026 Subscription along with Duromina from Agaro

items.title: Danche Hydro Honey
items.desc: We're welcoming in a new lot that we haven't worked with this producer before, and we've got to say - it's something very special! This is from the Danche Washing Station, in Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, very closely located to the Chelbesa stations. The cherry here is sourced from 810 registered growers in the villages Danche and Kubi, in Gedeo zone, Gedeb. The average elevation of the farms lies at around 2100 Meters Above Sea level on rich and fertile red soil in a semi-forested environment, and harvest takes place between November and January. items.title: Kiandu AA Washed
items.desc:
Great, classic washed Kenyan coffees are getting harder and harder to find unfortunately. Subtle changes to farming practices, environmental reasons, and changes to varieties mean that the classic Kenyan profile of old is much more rare. This Kiandu AA lot is a great representation of how great and fruity Kenyan Washed coffees can be!

items.desc:
Ever since first trying Ivan and Priscilla's coffee's in 2022, we loved what they produced. Their elusive Washed Geisha is a rare lot that speaks for itself in quality and elegance - something super special, and worth appreciating!
Grown in Bambito, nearby Volcan in Panama (just off the road leading to Cerro Punta), the land where their geisha grows goes up the mountain to around 1800m above sea level. items.title: Alo Main Station Dark Room Dry Natural
items.desc:
From the main station of Alo Village, and a producer we've worked with for several years now, comes a very special lot that represents how much Tamiru Tadesse has pushed processing at Alo. This lot is a classic natural, without extra fermentation but has a special dark room drying. Tamiru built these dark rooms for drying coffee a few years ago, but has expanded them recently to accomodate more lots, and we were lucky enough to get this one, lot #34. This whole 17kg lot has been sent to us, and we're happy to share it with you now.

items.title: Mama Sierra Caturra Washed
items.desc:
This is your answer to a daily coffee that's good on price, giving a dependable flavour profile, and enjoyable every day without being too much. Mama Sierra, led by Sirley Pulgarin of The Coffee Quest Colombia, is a remarkable project empowering women coffee farmers in the community of Giraldo, Antioquia. With 15 motivated members, the project began in March 2021, initiated by Yessica Parra and later taken forward by Sirley. The goal has always been to break barriers limiting women’s access to resources and training in coffee production.

items.title: Kotowa Las Brujas Geisha Clean Natural
items.desc:
This year is the first year we're buying from Kotowa Farms in Boquete, and we're absolutely thrilled to offer this amazing Geisha from their Las Brujas farm lot 26-094!
This lot in particular is their outstanding Geisha, which was processed with a "Natural" process, although the result in the cup is something that reminds us much more of a washed. We had confirmed with the farm that it was infact a natural, even though it does appear more washed. items.title: Chilaka Anaerobic Natural
items.desc:
Tamiru Tadesse is a coffee supplier who has been in the coffee business for the last eight years. He works with about 200 farmers in Delo Kebele, Bensa zone of the Sidama region. He collects about 182,000 kilograms of red cherry from an estimated 80 hectares of land owned by the farmers. Tamiru processes anaerobic and natural coffee which is dried on a raised bed with mesh wire. He then sells his coffee on the international market, mostly in China. However, he says, he was interested to have new market destinations and promote the unique flavours of Bensa coffee.

items.title: Altieri Pre-dry Natural Geisha DFM
items.desc:
This is our first year visiting and buying from the Altieri farm in Boquete, and it was an absolute treat. Getting to see their facilities, and cup their outstanding lots from a variety of processes and elevations is really impressive! We purchased a few lots from them, and the first to be released is this pre-dry natural Geisha.
This lot is from their Tom lot - it sits around 1700m above sea level at Alto Quiel, in Boquete, Panama. It covers an area of approximately 1 hectare of volcanic soil where Geisha Green Tip grows. It is adjacent to the protected area of the Volcan Baru national park,

items.title: Guji Rassa Washed
items.desc:
This is a classic washed Ethiopian coffee that ticks all the boxes. You can imagine that when someone says "washed Ethiopian coffee" you have a profile in mind - this is exactly that - nothing more, nothing less.
Grown from 2000-2200masl in the village of Rassa, in the Guji region of Ethiopia, this lot is comprised of mixed heirloom varieties without specific selection of varieties that comes with several smallholder farmers producing cherries at a time. The cherries are sent to the Suke Washing station where they're processed in the traditional washed fashion - floated, depulped, washed, and

items.title: El Dragón Sugarcane Decaf
items.desc:
A clean, sweet, Colombian decaf from the Santa Maria community in Huila. This is the kind of decaf we like to have around: easy to brew, comfortable to drink, and still very much tasting like good coffee.
This lot comes from the work of 25 smallholder producers in Santa Maria. The coffees are grown at 1700-2100m and built from Caturra, Pink Bourbon, Castillo, and Colombia varieties.

items.title: Chiroso Washed Las Perlitas
items.desc:
A washed Chiroso from Las Perlitas in Antioquia, Colombia, sourced through Coffee Quest. Smallholder deliveries are cupped separately and combined when their profiles complement one another.
Bright, juicy and sweet, with orange, prune and almond in the cup. We roast it to work beautifully as both filter and espresso.

items.title: Cherry Ripe Blend
notes: While it will still remain Clean
items.desc:
This coffee is born out of a simple question - how can we make an espresso blend that's the most fruity as possible, while still being clear and clean. We have been working on this lot for several months, starting right from sourcing. We worked hand in hand with our friends at Cofinet to source these components and design this blend around 3 particular lots.
Firstly a Washed and Natural Caturra - these set the base for our blend providing a fruity, yet well structured base. The last component is a small amount of a Cherry co-fermented coffee from Jairo Arcilla. This is what gives us that big b

items.title: Rose Rejects
items.desc:
Rose Rejects is coffee that didn’t make it into our main lineup.
It’s a mix of beans rejected by our colour sorter — including quakers and beans that are visually over-roasted — alongside roasted batches that missed our internal targets by being too light, too dark, or otherwise outside spec. Nothing unsafe, nothing adulterated, just coffee that didn’t meet the standard we set for Rose.
This is not a curated blend and it’s not meant to be expressive or particularly tasty. Expect a very basic cup. Sometimes flat, sometimes rough, sometimes fine — but never special. If you’re looking for clarity

items.title: The House Blend
items.desc:
This is a special "House Blend" that we've designed specifically for use on Espresso machines / Bialetti. It's an easy drinking coffee that has a well developed roast profile to make it easy to extract, while still keeping recognisable flavours of the origins. We would call this a "Medium - Dark" roast. Not so much that the beans are all oily, but developed enough to have Low Acidity, Smooth Body, and mostly chocolatey flavour notes.
All the coffees we use in this are Specialty coffee, but with very approachable taste profiles and qualities. We've sourced these lots either direct from farmers,

items.title: The Bedtime Blend
items.desc:
This is a blend that we've designed especially to be as delicious as non-decaffeinated coffee - to be used for Espresso/Bialetti brewing and goes amazing as both a black coffee, and with milk.
We believe that decaffeinated coffee doesn't have to come at the sacrifice of quality - so we created this Decaf blend that is as delicious as full strength coffee. Generally you will find more sweetness and acidity, as the balance with the bitter caffeine has been removed. In some of these coffees we find more spice, and malt notes from the decaf process, and some darker roasted notes from the darker ro

items.title: Jingle Beans Holiday Blend
items.desc: Behold! A coffee is born. 'Tis the freaking season and what have you! Oh, Jingle Beans, oh Jingle Beans, our annual ho-li-day blend. Each year we go out of our way to make this blend as seasonally outlandish as we can. This year, two coffees from Ethiopia — a washed and a naturally processed — triumphantly coalesce into the best interpretation of drinkable fruit cake in a cup. Jingle Beans, Jingle Beans, Jingle all the beans.

items.title: David Muñoz - Honduras
items.desc: For the second consecutive year, we kick off Honduran season with a coffee from David Muñoz, a producer who’s been a mainstay on the Tandem menu for a decade. David grows multiple varieties on his roughly 3 hectare farm, Nueva Esperanza, in Santa Barbara, but the majority is Pacas. This 100% Pacas lot is soft and sweetness-driven. We taste a familiar, balanced cup with flavors of caramel, milk chocolate, toasted nuts, and gentle plum-like acidity.

items.title: Arley Arboleda - Colombia
items.desc: This small lot from Arley Arboleda is another excellent Chiroso from Urrao. Arley is a 36-year-old, second-generation producer growing Chiroso at 2,100 masl across two hectares. He learned coffee farming from his father as a teenager and purchased the land for Finca Los Guaicos in 2022 with the specific goal of cultivating exclusively Chiroso. As with many producers in the region, Arley uses the cochadas method, a regional processing practice in which each day’s harvest is depulped and added to the same fermentation tank throughout the week. Once the tank is full, the coffee is washed together

items.title: Chelbesa - Ethiopia
items.desc: We’re excited to have back on our menu for another season this bright, refreshing classic from the Chelbesa One Washing Station. Approximately 1,000 smallholder farmers deliver cherry to Chelbesa One, one of seven washing stations across Ethiopia managed by SNAP Coffee. Cherries are sorted, floated, and depulped, then dry fermented in tanks for 48-72 hours before being washed and placed to dry on raised beds for 7-10 days. Coffees from this station are typically pristine and elegant. Expect a crisp, lightly effervescent profile with white tea aromatics and flavors of grapefruit, melon, and pea

items.title: Kibingo - Kenya
items.desc: This washed field blend from Kibingo Estate is another stellar coffee sourced via Kamavindi Coffee Labs. Established in 1957 with just 100 trees — the maximum allotment for Kenyan growers under colonial law at the time — Kibingo has since grown into one of the country’s most highly regarded estate farms. The estate won Kenya’s Taste of Harvest competition in 2024, and owner Anthony Kimani has continued investing in farm-level and processing infrastructure, with plans to expand beyond its current 6,000 trees. In the cup, we taste ripe red fruits like pomegranate and raspberry, sweet spice, and

items.title: Oneska - Kenya
items.desc: Oneska is the small estate farm of Onesmus Njagi, a retired schoolteacher, and his wife, Karen, on the slopes of Mount Kenya in Embu County. Last fall, we visited ahead of harvest and toured their four hectares, where they grow the traditional SL-28 and SL-34 varieties at good altitude and under ideal growing conditions. The name Oneska is a portmanteau of Onesmus and Karen, who established the farm in the early 1990s and have spent decades honing their agronomic and processing practices. They process their coffee using the classic Kenyan “double fermentation”: 20 hours of dry fermentation fol

items.title: Heri Agena - Ethiopia
items.desc: This microlot is the first of four coffees we’ll feature this year from Karamo Coffee, a quality-driven export company working in the high-altitude regions of Bensa and Bura in Sidama. We met Teddy of Karamo in Addis Ababa last year for a quick cupping and were very impressed by the quality of the coffees on the table. items.title: Danche Yellow Honey- Ethiopia
items.desc: This honey-processed Ethiopian coffee comes to us from Danche station in Gedeb, one of two sites operated by SNAP Specialty Coffee in the kebele of Chelbesa. Founded in 2019, Danche now processes cherry from approximately 800 nearby smallholder farmers, most of whom grow small amounts of coffee on 2-3 hectare plots of land at significant elevation. Danche began with a focus on washed lots but has since expanded to include natural, honey, and experimental preparations. items.title: Alma Pineda - Cup of Excellence - Honduras
items.desc: This year, we purchased a split share of Alma Pineda’s washed Gesha lot, one of our top-scoring coffees from the 2026 Honduras Cup of Excellence (CoE). Alma’s coffees have placed at the Honduras CoE before, including third in 2019 and second in 2024, with this lot placing eighth in the Exotic Varieties category. Her farm, El Limo, sits at 1650 masl in Santa Barbara, where nearly all the Honduran coffee on our menu is grown. items.title: Young Hunting - True Believers (Aqua Blue Vinyl)
items.desc:

Hazel has been in rotation at Little Tandem for years thanks to Ilya Mxx (guitar and vox) who sent me a copy soon after its release. Ilya lived on my floor freshman year of college. He lured me into his dorm room on the first day of school by blasting Nada Surf with the door open. Back then he could perfectly play all of the guitar parts on Pinkerton from memory. It was no surprise to me when Young Hunting turned out to be amazing. - Will

The Good Thing selection for August 2018.
Another Little Tandem staple from way back in the day. This album was originally given to me by my good friend and coffee expert Dillon Edwards back when were both honing our coffee skills at Blue Bottle Coffee. Dillon had 2 copies for some reason and gave me his extra. In return I gave him my extra copy of Louis’ Hello Dolly . I think I got the better end of the deal for this record is a true masterpiece. Full of stories, life lessons and and heavy themes like “Cocaine”, “Vietnam” and “The Reason Young People Use Drugs”, one or 2 copies of this record

items.title: Sun Lamp Decaf
items.desc:
“I might as well be drinking tea*,” you say to no one in particular as you drink another cup of lousy decaffeinated coffee. Don’t feel defeated by bad decaf. Turn to Tandem’s brighter, sweeter Sun Lamp. With hints of marshmallow, graham cracker and green grape, let the surprising flavors of Sun Lamp reimagine what decaffeinated coffee can be and leave the anxiety behind.
*No offense to tea. We love tea.

items.title: West End Blues
items.desc: Traditional in name only, West End Blues is a complex blend of flavors and textures. Fruity but not fruit-forward, grounded in chocolate and sparkling with zesty notes of baking spices and tea, WEB shines when combined with milk but stands on its own as a killer drip coffee.

items.title: Stoker
items.desc: Sometimes you want a delicious, no-nonsense cup of coffee, beloved by metalheads and hardcore grandmothers alike. That’s why Tandem shed its “Light Roaster” mantle to create our version of a “Kinda Dark” roasted coffee. Inspired by late-night diner runs, hot donuts, and arctic blasts, Stoker’s pleasantly sweet roastiness will carry you through the day.

items.title: Time & Temperature
items.desc: Effervescent, electric, and just plain cool, Time and Temperature is Tandem’s signature espresso blend. Perfect for dancing alone or with friends, it doubles as a delightful drip coffee. However you enjoy its crisp acidity and punchy sweetness, it’s our embodiment of “Spreading Joy” in every cup.
